# A04 — AUDIT: Broker interface, authentication and broker state

**Status:** APPROVED — the AUDIT of topic A04 (Document 04, section 4, step 6), approved by Rama on 2026-11-14 with the A04 topic package (Decision Register, D-33); where it and the RECONCILED TOPIC RECORD differ, the record governs
**Date:** 2026-11-13
**Revision history:** First version, 2026-11-13 (fieldwork of 12 and 13-Nov-2026, on the AUDIT requirements of ChatGPT's A04 investigation direction of 11-Nov-2026, begun after ChatGPT's full review of the revised A04 STUDY passed on 12-Nov-2026 and Rama's go-ahead of the same day). Corrected, 2026-11-13, after ChatGPT's review of the same day (not passed; two document corrections): section 1.3's credentials bullet made consistent with section 19 (`config/accounts.csv` read only for its column names and variable names; no `.env`, token, key or overlay file opened), and section 19's last bullet now records the assembled-document checks as completed before submission; no ID, result, count or register entry changed. Approved by Rama on 2026-11-14 with the A04 topic package (Decision Register, D-33): status marked APPROVED; content unchanged.
**Purpose and scope:** The comparison of what the legacy code actually does with what was intended, for the entire A04 scope of the Master System Investigation Index: the construction, selection and configuration of the broker client and the adapters; runtime authentication, the token lifecycle, the token monitor, the authentication classifier and the clock-skew probe; the token tooling outside the trading process; the Zerodha adapter's order actions, retries and uncertain outcomes, its reads and its translation of broker state; every non-test caller's use of the broker interface; rate limits and concurrency; the order monitor and the order state machine; product resolution and the position helpers; and costs, slippage and the tick helpers, with every normal, refused, error, timeout, rate-limit, retry, restart, concurrency and shutdown flow, at the fixed baseline. It audits the STUDY's 26 AUDIT points, its UNKNOWN items, its 13 duplication rows, its findings on documents and records, the 58 items handed to A04 and the A04 scope beyond them, records each result (MATCH, ISSUE or UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED) with its evidence, and decides nothing.
**Source:** trading-system-prod-snapshot, branch `main`, commit `970aabf3c78d777d9d34549e021f7c8e756c7bdb` (Source Inventory, SRC-10), read from the local read-only clone on 12 and 13-Nov-2026; nothing in it was written or run.
**Related documents:** Documents 04, 06, 07, 08 and 10; the Master System Investigation Index (entry A04); the Decision Register, D-07, D-12, D-17, D-21, D-23 to D-25, D-28 and D-30 to D-32; ChatGPT's A04 investigation direction of 11-Nov-2026 and its review of the A04 STUDY of 12-Nov-2026 (not kept as files, D-17); the A04 STUDY (`A04_STUDY_2026-11-12.md`) and its evidence; `evidence/A04_AUDIT_INTENT_SOURCES_2026-11-12.md`; the A01, A02 and A03 AUDITs and RECONCILED TOPIC RECORDs, the Open Issues Register and the Audit Findings Register.

## 1. Purpose, scope, exclusions, baseline and method

### 1.1 Purpose

This is the AUDIT of topic A04 (Document 04, section 4, step 6; Document 07, section 5). For every A04 area and flow it compares the actual behaviour, established by the STUDY and re-checked here against the code, with the intended behaviour found in the admitted sources, and records matches, issues and UNKNOWN items (Document 04, section 5.4). It classifies; it does not decide. Every issue is raised with Rama after ChatGPT's review (Document 04, section 5.5); no treatment and no V2 design is proposed here.

### 1.2 Scope

The scope is the STUDY's (its sections 1.2 and 3 to 12, and its source file inventory): the twelve files under `broker/` (`zerodha_adapter.py`, `rate_limiter.py`, `order_monitor.py`, `order_state_machine.py`, `token_monitor.py`, `auth_recovery.py`, `product_resolver.py`, `cost_calculator.py`, `slippage_engine.py`, `clock_skew_probe.py`, `position_helpers.py` and `angelone_adapter.py`), `deploy/token_watcher.sh`, `deploy/zerodha_morning.bat` and `deploy/zerodha_morning.ps1`, `scripts/auto_refresh_token.py`, `scripts/copy_token_to_vm.bat` and `scripts/zerodha_login.py`, with the broker side of every non-test caller of the broker interface and of the boundary files that other topics own (`config/broker_costs.yaml`, `config/broker_limits.yaml`, `config/slippage_model.yaml`, the token watcher's unit, the pre-flight broker check, the end-of-day broker reconcile script). Section 2 shows the coverage by area and file, by flow, by STUDY AUDIT point, by STUDY UNKNOWN item, by duplication row and for the documents and records.

### 1.3 Exclusions and ownership boundaries

- Callers' business logic belongs to the owner topics: the system order lifecycle and order placement to A10, exit and trade management to A11, end-of-day and reconciliation workflows to A12, kill-switch and recovery control to A13, capital and sizing to A09, instrument and market-data acquisition to A05, orchestration, start-up and the time authority to A01, configuration sources, schemas, defaults and precedence to A02, the storage implementation to A03, reports to A15 and schedule declarations and invocation to A16. This AUDIT records the broker call, the contract the caller receives and how the caller uses it, names the owner, and hands the rest over (each part's section .5, and section 15). A finding inside another topic's code is a handoff and is not counted as an A04 ISSUE; A04 records and counts its own part.
- A01's, A02's and A03's findings are not re-classified: their IDs, classifications, statuses and treatments are unchanged, and A04 records only its own part (section 4). An AGREED new-system treatment is a Phase 2 input, never evidence of what the legacy system was meant to do. A03's item G-19 is cited by its ID only.
- Credentials (D-07 and Rama's standing instruction): no credential-validity, credential-history or exposure investigation is made, and no alert, issue or recommendation about it; `config/accounts.csv` was read only for its column names and the environment-variable names it lists, and no account identifier or credential value from it was used for any checking purpose or reproduced; no `.env` file, token file, key file or `*.local.yaml` overlay was opened; credential variable names and file paths are recorded as configuration only (section 19, security restriction). The functional audit of authentication (how a token is created, stored by path pattern, loaded, validated, refreshed, expired, invalidated and recovered) is in scope.
- Scheduling: cron and systemd declarations are boundary facts; no declaration is taken as proof that a job ran.
- Tests belong to A19 and are cited only as evidence of intent or behaviour, never as proof of runtime behaviour.
- Paper-only paths are not audited (live-only project); they are marked where a Live and a paper branch split.
- No repair of the legacy system, no treatment and no V2 design.

### 1.4 Baseline

Every line reference is to commit `970aabf3c78d777d9d34549e021f7c8e756c7bdb` (D-21). Before and after every helper's work on 12 and 13-Nov-2026, `git rev-parse HEAD` in the clone returned it and `git status --short` was empty (each part's section .1).

### 1.5 Method

- Rama approved the use of helpers for A04 on 11-Nov-2026 ("Helpers, with saved progress (Recommended)"; Topic Completion Register, entry A04), as in A01 to A03. The audit was done by AI helpers under the same read-only rules as the STUDY: one for the intended-behaviour sources (the evidence file `evidence/A04_AUDIT_INTENT_SOURCES_2026-11-12.md`) and ten audit parts, each with its own prefix: CL (client construction, selection, configuration, the adapter contracts and the AngelOne stub), AU (runtime authentication, token use, the token monitor, the authentication classifier and clock skew), TT (the token tooling outside the trading process), OA (the adapter's order actions, exception translation, retries and uncertain outcomes), RD (the adapter's reads and the translation of broker state), CS (the broker call-site map: every caller's use of the broker interface), RL (rate limits and concurrency), MO (the order monitor and the order state machine), PR (product resolution and the position helpers) and CG (costs, slippage and the tick helpers). Each helper saved its work after every item, so that a stop lost no finished work (helpers were stopped twice by the AI usage limit and three times by session or server restarts); stopped helpers were resumed from their saved progress, and the work in progress was backed up to the temporary branch of algocore_system that Rama allowed on 11-Nov-2026 (never merged; deleted once the A04 STUDY and AUDIT are on `main`).
- Every part and the evidence file went through three passes by three different helpers: a writer, an independent checker that re-read every record against the code and the cited sources, and a corrector that settled each finding against the code. A further helper, which had written none of the parts, then checked the nine corrected parts other than CG against each other for duplicates, contradictions, consistency of treatment, coverage, totals, identifiers and security; a fifth helper applied its decisions; and a sixth checked part CG against the nine applied parts in the same way and applied its results (section 1.8). Claude made the decisions that the checks left to the coordinator (section 1.8) and assembled this document.
- Each part re-read every cited line at the baseline with `git show`, `git grep`, `git log` and `git blame`, and with its own scripts, kept outside the clone and run with `python3 -I`. Python and library behaviour was tested only with generic code written by the helpers (no legacy code and no legacy import), on Python 3.13.18; such results are INTERPRETATION. The `kiteconnect` library is not in the repository: what depends on its behaviour is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED unless the repository itself shows it. Tests were read as documents only. Nothing in the clone was written, run or imported, and no broker call, login, token refresh, deployment script or cron job was run. Every repository-wide search excluded the account file, environment files, local overlays and token files; once, before that exclusion was made general, a repository-wide search displayed rows of two such files on a helper's screen (part AU, section 6.1), and in part TT some broad read-only views of legacy text showed identifier text on a helper's screen (section 7.1); nothing from them was copied, recorded or used.
- Intended behaviour was sought in every admitted source: module and method docstrings, comments, log and alert texts, configuration keys and comments, `docs/locked_decisions.yaml`, the broker integration audit and the other legacy audit and decision documents, design documents, runbooks and operator cards, the system map, `config/expected_managers.yaml` (a declaration frozen on 01-Aug-2026), commit messages and the existing technical records, and the approved A01, A02 and A03 records and Rama's recorded decisions. Every legacy source is HISTORICAL. Where sources conflict, both are recorded and none is chosen; where no source states the intent, the record says "not established" and audits the code on its own (Document 04, section 5.3).

### 1.6 Record fields, results, classifications and the KNOWN DEFECT rule

- Record fields (Document 04, section 5.4; Document 10, section 7): area and flow; issue category (Document 04, section 5.3); intended behaviour and its source (path and lines or key, with its date), or "not established"; the actual code path; the actual behaviour and the effective value; the evidence (STUDY evidence statement IDs and code lines); the result and its classification; the severity or impact where established; the owner topic; the cross-reference to the STUDY point or question and to any A01, A02 or A03 item; and whether Rama's intent or decision is needed. Issues and UNKNOWN items are blocks (each part's section .3); matches are table rows with the same information in short form (each part's section .4).
- Results, as in the A01 to A03 AUDITs (their section 1.6): MATCH (the code does what the sources intend); ISSUE (a difference from intended behaviour; a conflict between sources that the code resolves one way; or, where intent is not established, a defect or weakness that the code itself demonstrates, of a kind that Document 04, section 5.3 lists, the basis being named in the record); UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (the answer needs runtime evidence that does not survive, or intent is not established and the code demonstrates no such defect or weakness). A lack of intent evidence alone does not make an ISSUE. An item with a MATCH part and an ISSUE part is counted as ISSUE. WITHDRAWN records keep their IDs with a cross-reference note and are not counted. Hard-coded operating values against the project rules (`docs/foundation_engineering_rules.md` 1.4 and 1.9) are classed ISSUE (minor; weakness: hard-coded values), with a MATCH part where their own source gives the value, as A01 C23 (ISSUE), MO-46 and AU-07 class such literals.
- Classifications (Document 04, section 6): FACT, INTERPRETATION, HISTORICAL, KNOWN DEFECT, OPEN QUESTION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED.
- The KNOWN DEFECT rule is the A01 AUDIT's, section 1.6, applied unchanged: (a) the code implements a mechanism for the case; (b) by the language or library semantics that mechanism fails for certain whenever the case occurs; (c) the case is one that the code or an intent source says it handles, and it can arise under the documented set-up; (d) the outcome contradicts every intent source found. Each record that gives or considers KNOWN DEFECT states which conditions hold and which fails. Every KNOWN DEFECT is provisional until ChatGPT's review and the issue discussion with Rama. Where a prior topic's KNOWN DEFECT has an A04 side (A03 R-04 in MO-04), its classification stays the prior topic's and is not counted again as A04's.

### 1.7 Identifiers and conventions

- CL-nn, AU-nn, TT-nn, OA-nn, RD-nn, CS-nn, RL-nn, MO-nn, PR-nn and CG-nn are this AUDIT's items in parts CL (section 5), AU (6), TT (7), OA (8), RD (9), CS (10), RL (11), MO (12), PR (13) and CG (14). Within each part the issue and UNKNOWN items are numbered first and the match rows after them; items added by a corrector, and match rows moved to ISSUE after a check, keep or continue the sequence. The two-letter prefixes do not collide with A01's (C, S, W, M, B), A02's (L, V, T, F, K, X) or A03's (D, H, N, P, Q, R, U, Y, E, G, J, Z) item IDs; prior topics' IDs are always named with their topic. They are not the legacy labels (for example BL-6, ZA3, RL6, OM11, CC12, FIX-188, H-13) of the legacy documents.
- Inside sections 5 to 14, a reference to "section 1" to "section 7" without a document name means that part's own subsection (for example, inside section 8, "section 5" is section 8.5). A part's own lower-level subsections are written with their full number in this AUDIT (for example "section 10.2.1"), and a reference to another part names the part or gives this AUDIT's section number (for example "part RD, section 5" or "section 9.5"). Every other section reference names its document, or is to this AUDIT where the number has a dot and is outside 5 to 14.
- IS-, IC-, CD- and RS-numbers are those of the evidence file `evidence/A04_AUDIT_INTENT_SOURCES_2026-11-12.md` (its sources, conflicts between sources, statements that only the code contradicts and statements attributed to Rama or the operator); the short names of legacy documents are those of that file. Pxx-Snnn are statement IDs of the STUDY's evidence files. "17.1 point n" is the STUDY's AUDIT point n, and "STUDY question n" its question n (section 18 of the STUDY).
- The helpers' synthetic tests are named T1, T2 and so on, without a hyphen; they are not item IDs.
- Security: credential values, tokens, account identifiers, personal names, e-mail addresses, IP addresses, fingerprints and absolute home paths are never written; per-account names are written with `<ACCOUNT_ID>`, and passages that hold such material are cited by path and line only.
- Line references are written "L123" or "L123 to L130"; dates as 2026-11-13 or 13-Nov-2026.

### 2.2 By flow

An item is listed under a flow only when its record's "Area and flow" or "Actual behaviour and effective value" field (for a match row, its area and actual-behaviour cells) names that route; the KNOWN DEFECT condition clauses and the other fields are not used. Selected by script on those fields, with the keywords that each flow's description names, and read for loose matches (the CNC lock and the single-instance lock, for example, are not counted as concurrency; the disposition words 'REJECTED as an issue', 'frozen' data classes and registries, the file name `refresh_instruments.py` and alert texts are not counted as routes); "normal" holds the items that name none of the other routes. An item can fall under several flows. The flows follow STUDY sections 6 to 10 and this AUDIT's scope (header and section 1.2; normal, rejection, error, timeout and uncertain outcome, HTTP 429 and rate limit, retry, restart and rehydration, concurrency, token expiry and recovery, shutdown, and empty, malformed and partial responses).

## 3. Intended-behaviour sources and conflicts

The inventory is the evidence file `evidence/A04_AUDIT_INTENT_SOURCES_2026-11-12.md`, committed with this AUDIT (written by a helper, checked by a second and corrected by a third, then completed at the cross-part assembly). It holds 131 sources by area (IS-01 to IS-131): (a) broker selection, client construction, the adapter abstraction and contracts, the Angel One stub and `system.broker`, 15 (IS-01 to IS-12, IS-124, IS-130 and IS-131); (b) the order actions, 18 (IS-13 to IS-30); (c) the reads and the translation of broker state, 10 (IS-31 to IS-39, IS-128); (d) rate limits and concurrency, 15 (IS-40 to IS-53, IS-129); (e) the order monitor and the order state machine, 18 (IS-54 to IS-70, IS-122); (f) authentication and the token lifecycle in the trading process, 11 (IS-71 to IS-80, IS-123); (g) clock skew, 7 (IS-81 to IS-87); (h) the token tooling outside the process, 11 (IS-88 to IS-98); (i) product resolution and positions, 8 (IS-99 to IS-106); (j) costs, slippage and tick handling, 11 (IS-107 to IS-114, IS-125 to IS-127); (k) the existing technical records, 7 (IS-115 to IS-121). IS-131, `config/expected_managers.yaml` (a HISTORICAL declaration, frozen 01-Aug-2026), was found by part CS and added at the cross-part assembly; it bears on the wiring records of part CS and on the stale constructor-line references (section 2.6). The file also holds 31 conflicts between sources (IC-01 to IC-31), 45 statements that only the code contradicts (CD-01 to CD-48, with CD-10, CD-24 and CD-28 withdrawn and moved to IC-12, IC-20 and IC-23), and 14 statements attributed to Rama or the operator (RS-01 to RS-14).

The source families searched: `docs/locked_decisions.yaml` in full for broker, token, rate-limit, product, cost and order-state decisions (G4, G7, RL1 to RL10, CC1 to CC12, PR1 to PR10 and the principles block among them); the v2 design specification and the module instructions (M11, M13, M14, M33, M34, M38, M41); the legacy design, decision, audit, incident and runbook documents and the operator procedures; the configuration files and their comments (`config/system_config.yaml`, `config/broker_limits.yaml`, `config/broker_costs.yaml`, `config/slippage_model.yaml`) and the cron registry and units as declarations (A16, A17); the docstrings, comments, names, log and alert texts of the A04 files and of their boundary files, with the design labels they cite (ZA1 to ZA17, TM1 to TM7, OM1 to OM12, OSM1 to OSM14, PR1 to PR10, CC1 to CC12, BL-6, BL-19, BL-21, FIX-nnn); commit messages; the five existing technical records (as sources IS-115 to IS-121, with the records check's results); and the project records (the A01, A02 and A03 intent-sources files, the Open Issues Register and Rama's recorded history answers). Tests were not read (A19). Every legacy source is HISTORICAL: documentary evidence of what someone intended or believed at its date, never proof that anything was installed, ran or was in force (Document 08, section 10); runtime claims inside sources (measured counts, "VERIFIED LIVE", captured broker books) are UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED. The records cite the sources they rely on.

The 31 conflicts are listed below with the items whose records rely on them; none is chosen here. Where a later source names and replaces an earlier one, the evidence file says so ("later, names ..."); the code's side is stated in the records.

Statements that only the code contradicts (CD-01 to CD-48; 45 counted). No other admitted source states a different intent for them; the legacy audits that record the same gap describe the code and state no other intent. Among them: the adapter as the only module that touches `kiteconnect` (CD-01; CL-01, AU-06), ZA2's frozen results (CD-02), HTTP-library timeouts as broker timeouts (CD-05; OA-01, OA-02), the in-flight recovery that cannot run under `main.py`'s wiring (CD-06; OA-08, CS-08), the 429 handling of cancels and modifications (CD-07; OA-05, OA-20), the live margin read (CD-08; RD-10, CS-07), the GTT 429s reported as placements (CD-09; OA-06, RD-01), the forward-shadow "SAME broker RateLimiter" (CD-11; RL-06), `_VALID_CATEGORIES` (CD-12; RL-08), the margins-bucket remark (CD-13; RL-07), the token monitor outside the limiter (CD-14; AU-06), OM1's EXPIRED (CD-15; MO-24), OM5's quantity rule (CD-16; MO-02), OM11's counter (CD-17; MO-07), the rejection text (CD-18; MO-03), the COMPLETE payload (CD-19; MO-04), the once-per-day force close (CD-20; MO-17), the rehydration's bring-forward (CD-21; MO-09), "Single source of truth" (CD-22; MO-23), the cancel finalisation (CD-23; MO-12), TM7 (CD-25; AU-14), the recovery after a token failure (CD-26; AU-11, AU-12, TT-24), "never blocked" (CD-29; TT-02), the refresh's credential names (CD-30; TT-09), the watcher's restart alert (CD-31; TT-15), `scripts\zerodha_morning.bat` (CD-32; TT-23), "Eliminates hardcoded" product strings (CD-33; PR-01, CG-30), `intent_for`'s stated user (CD-34; PR-05), the slippage helpers on Live paths (CD-36; CG-10, CG-11), "every order" and "the paper engine" (CD-37, CD-38; CG-01), the `.invalid` rename (CD-42; AU-12), "validation before rate_limiter.acquire" (CD-43; OA-10, OA-25, RD-14), "must be > 0" (CD-44; CG-02) and "(Pydantic, immutable)" (CD-45; PR-03). The others rest on the same records by subject or are mapped in section 2.6: CD-03 and CD-04 (the design's broker abstraction and the stub's "same interface"; CL-17, CL-16), CD-46 to CD-48 (the timeout closure records, ZA14's import list and IC9's `account_id`; CL-08, CL-03, CL-04), CD-27 and CD-35 (the probe's tier comment and `main.py`'s product-map remark; section 2.6), and CD-39 to CD-41 (the records' token-validation, cost-calculator and state-machine descriptions; section 2.6; CD-41 also CS-30 and MO-23).

Statements attributed to Rama or the operator (RS-01 to RS-14). RS-01 to RS-04 are this project's own records of Rama's answers in the Open Issues Register (A01-01 to A01-04, 05-Nov-2026: headless operation; a missing credential variable meant to give exit 5; `accounts.csv` kept for a manual choice of client, the system meant to use one configured Zerodha client; no indefinite restarts); they are intent evidence as recorded, and the agreed treatments of those entries are Phase 2 inputs, not legacy intent. RS-05 to RS-14 are HISTORICAL documentary statements in legacy files and commits (the market-protection band values, the M41 "locked" decisions on the browser login and the token record, the Q4 invariant, the netting ruling of 03-Aug, the net-P&L status, the morning resume of 20-Jun, the rollback record's inference, the power outage, the 08:15 role assignment and the contract-note status); where a passage is a role assignment, a status or an event rather than a statement of intent, the evidence file says so, and the events are UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED as runtime facts. Rama's other recorded history answers that bear on A04 are OPEN and are not intent evidence: A01-08, A01-11 and A01-19 (no historical answer), A01-15, A01-18 and A01-24 ("Rama does not remember"), A02-10, A02-12, A02-15 and A03-34 ("Rama answered OPEN", 08-Nov to 11-Nov-2026); A01-25's history was not asked; A01-03's exit-code history stays OPEN (RS-03 records only Rama's statement of the file's purpose). No other statement by Rama about A04 behaviour is recorded in the registers or in the evidence file; his standing instruction on credential material (D-07) governs only what this AUDIT may examine.

A point that bears on every comparison with production: every file, value and declaration in this AUDIT is the one at the baseline. Which commit and which files were in force on either machine, which account and key were used, and whether any declared job ran, are UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (Document 08, section 10; section 19).

### 5.3 Issue and UNKNOWN records

##### CL-01 — The adapter's "single point of contact" claims against thirteen other kiteconnect importers and the raw-client flows

- **Area and flow:** the broker boundary as a whole: which modules import `kiteconnect` or reach the Kite client outside the adapter's methods, in the trading process and in the scripts.
- **Issue category:** Documentation against code; Consistency across components.
- **Intended behaviour and source:** (1) Exclusivity: `broker/zerodha_adapter.py` L4 to L7 ("Single point of contact with the Zerodha kiteconnect SDK. No other module in the codebase imports kiteconnect directly."), ZA1 L10 to L11 ("No direct kiteconnect import anywhere else in the codebase"), L95 and the class docstring L347 to L349 ("All broker I/O flows through this class; no other module touches kiteconnect directly (ZA1)"), all 17-Apr-2026 (`bcf03b5`); `docs/web_claude/01_module_instructions/module_13_zerodha_adapter.txt` L4 to L5 and ZA1 L9 to L10 (17-Apr-2026); `scripts/preflight/__init__.py` L19 (21-Jun-2026, `3cb17fe`): "Broker calls go through broker/zerodha_adapter only". (2) Sources of the same date that require other importers: MAIN19 (`module_34_main.txt` L359 to L363, 17-Apr-2026: `main.py` builds `KiteConnect(...)`); LF8 (`docs/locked_decisions.yaml` L2488 to L2495, lines 17-Apr-2026: the live feed "Imports: kiteconnect (KiteTicker)"); `docs/v2_design_spec.md` L419 (17-Apr-2026: "auth/zerodha_login.py → (kiteconnect) [external]"); the same spec maps `data/live_feed.py` to `broker/zerodha_adapter` instead (L424, 17-Apr-2026), against LF8, so the design documents also conflict among themselves. (3) Later sources that accept raw-client use without naming ZA1: `main.py` L395 to L402 (27-Jun-2026, `dea336a`: "Live: reuse kite_client (== adapter._kite)" for read-only historical data); `broker/token_monitor.py` L44 to L45 (30-May-2026, `0cd1b14`: `profile_fn=adapter._kite.profile`); `scripts/preflight/checks/broker.py` L7 to L9 (21-Jun-2026: the probe uses "the standalone pattern used by fetch_daily_candles"); commit `adc75c5` (13-Jun-2026, FIX-167) and `docs/audit/system_audit_14jun2026.md` L207 to L208 (F35, lines 13-Jun-2026): the adapter in `scripts/reconcile_pnl.py` and `scripts/reconcile_positions.py` "Replaced with direct KiteConnect client — scripts only need kite.positions(), not the full adapter" (a deliberate move of two scripts from the adapter to a raw client). No source names or replaces ZA1. HISTORICAL.
- **Actual code path:** importers (`git grep`, tests excluded): `main.py` L383, L409 and L486 (the last two paper-only), `data/live_feed.py` L18, and `scripts/eod_broker_reconcile.py` L219, `scripts/fetch_daily_candles.py` L275, `scripts/forward_shadow_record.py` L104, `scripts/gemini_data_integrity_check.py` L151, `scripts/preflight/checks/broker.py` L153, `scripts/reconcile_pnl.py` L97, `scripts/reconcile_positions.py` L149, `scripts/reconstruct_excursions.py` L286, `scripts/refresh_instruments.py` L297, `scripts/sr_corp_action_spotcheck.py` L35, `scripts/t2_cnc_gtt_realtest.py` L150; raw-client flows in the trading process: `main.py` L3389 (`broker_adapter._kite.profile` given to `TokenMonitor`) and L404 to L405, L421 to L438, L3480 to L3487 (the historical closure on the same object); the pre-flight probe `scripts/preflight/checks/broker.py` L127 to L158.
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: 13 non-test files besides the adapter import `kiteconnect`, with 15 import lines; the adapter's own L95 is prose and L109 its own import. FACT: inside the trading process two flows use the adapter's client outside its methods: the token monitor calls `profile` on `_kite` directly, and, when any feature gated at L3480 is enabled, the historical closure calls `historical_data` on the same object (L404 to L405 return `kite_client` in live). FACT: the pre-flight probe builds its own `KiteConnect` and calls `profile`, `margins` and `orders` on it (L131 to L138), against its own package docstring (L19). FACT (boundary, part TT): two scripts reach Kite's login and session endpoints without the SDK (`scripts/zerodha_login.py` L40 to L41, L104 to L112; `scripts/auto_refresh_token.py` L58 to L60). INTERPRETATION: ZA1 describes the client as "injected", which needs an importer outside the adapter, so the literal exclusivity could not hold even on ZA1's own design; under the narrower reading (no other module calls the broker through `kiteconnect`), the eleven script clients, the token monitor's call and the historical closure contradict it.
- **Evidence:** P01-S011 to P01-S014, P01-S032, P01-S084, P01-S096, P01-S193; P12-S089, P12-S199, P12-S200 (records R02-50, R02-57); the importer `git grep` and the code lines above.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE. FACT (importers and flows); HISTORICAL (claims); INTERPRETATION (the injection reading). Sources conflict: the exclusivity claims against MAIN19, LF8 and the design spec's dependency map of the same date, and against the later docstrings and records that accept raw use (item (3)); none names the other, so none is chosen, and the code follows no single rule. FACT: `_build_kite_client` reads both variables with `os.environ[...]` and has no emptiness test and no `try`; the pre-load raises `KeyError` (exit 6) only for an unset key variable or a token object without `access_token`, so a key variable that is set but empty, or an empty `access_token`, passes L2361 and L2363 and reaches `KiteConnect(api_key="")` or `set_access_token("")`. INTERPRETATION (code reading, with A01 C8 and C12): the boot's first broker call, the clock check, then runs with that client; an empty key is also reported by the required-secrets step (`missing_secrets`, exit 3) where the row's `api_key_env` is the convention name that L228 checks (`ZERODHA_API_KEY_<ACCOUNT_ID>`; true at the committed file values, A01 C12), while an empty token is refused locally only at the later gate (`scripts/zerodha_login.py` L76, `main.py` L2547), which is reached only if the clock check passed. ##### CL-06 — The Date-header hook: installed or skipped without a record, capturing from every response, with parse failures swallowed

- **Area and flow:** adapter construction; the hook on the shared client's HTTP session that feeds the broker clock (the read of the value is part AU's).
- **Issue category:** Observability; Failure handling (MATCH parts: intended against actual).
- **Intended behaviour and source:** FIX-009 (`broker/zerodha_adapter.py` L450 to L452 and docstring L1326 to L1332, both 12-May-2026, `31075d0`, commit "FIX-009: get_server_time uses HTTP Date header via response hook"): "capture the HTTP Date header from the most recent Kite API response so get_server_time() can return the broker's actual clock instead of the local RTT midpoint"; "capture the HTTP Date header from each Kite API response"; "If the attribute is absent (mocks, paper mode) the hook is silently skipped." The consumer's comment (L1712 to L1714, same commit): the hook "captures the HTTP Date header from this call". No source addresses an unparsable header or a record of installation. HISTORICAL.
- **Actual code path:** `ZerodhaAdapter.__init__` L453 to L454; `_install_date_header_hook` L1325 to L1352 (`_capture_date` L1341 to L1350); `main.py` L388 to L389 (the same session's `mount`, unguarded).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: the hook is installed once, from `__init__`, in either mode, whenever the client has a `reqsession` with `hooks`; otherwise it returns silently (L1334 to L1339); no log line records installation or skipping. FACT: `_capture_date` is appended to the session's `response` hooks (L1352); when called it takes a non-empty `Date` header, parses it and stores it as IST in `_last_response_date`; any exception in parsing is discarded (`except Exception: pass`, L1349 to L1350), leaving the previous value; the write takes no lock. INTERPRETATION (requests' hook semantics, outside the repository): every response of the shared client, on any thread and from any endpoint (error responses and, when a feature gated at `main.py` L3480 is enabled, the historical fetches), replaces the value, as the docstring's "each Kite API response" says. INTERPRETATION (narrowing P01-S147): a live boot reaches the adapter only after `kite.reqsession.mount(...)` succeeded at `main.py` L389, so in live the silent skip needs a session object without `hooks`; the skip is otherwise a mock or paper case, as the docstring states. FACT: a later reader cannot tell "no response yet", "no hook" and "unparsable header" apart (all leave `None` after `get_server_time`'s reset, L1715); the local-clock fallback that follows is part AU's (A01 C8, C30).
- **Evidence:** P01-S047 to P01-S052, P01-S147; P04-S361, P07-S112 (STUDY section 13 row "Broker clock"); the lines above; `git blame` (all hook lines `31075d0`).
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (observability; minor), with MATCH parts. FACT; INTERPRETATION (library semantics). MATCH: installation in both modes, capture from every response and the silent skip for mocks and paper are as the docstring states. ISSUE part: a header that fails to parse is discarded without a record, and nothing records whether the hook is active, so the clock check's fallback to the local clock cannot be told from a real broker reading (a weakness the code demonstrates; intent not established for these cases). KNOWN DEFECT not considered: no source says the hook handles or reports parse failures (condition (c) fails).
- **Severity or impact where established:** not established; whether the hook was installed and captured headers at run time is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (P01-S147). The cross-thread overwrite between `get_server_time`'s reset and read is handed to parts AU and RL (section 5).
- **Owner:** A04 (the hook); part AU (the reading and its fallback); part RL (concurrency on the shared session).
- **Cross-reference:** P01-S159 (point 8); STUDY 17.1 points 13 and 22; STUDY section 13 row "Broker clock" (part AU, pointer RL); A01 C8, C30, C38a; Open Issues Register A01-08, A01-15; CL-18; AU-16 (the unmarked fallback in `get_server_time`; distinct).
- **Rama:** not needed.

### 6.3 Issue and UNKNOWN records

##### AU-01 — `load_token` and `is_token_valid` against their contract: a non-UTF-8 file raises, non-object JSON is returned, and the validity test raises instead of answering "invalid"

- **Area and flow:** the token-file contract of `scripts/zerodha_login.py` as every caller uses it: the live start (pre-load, gate, third read), the in-process health endpoint (A15) and two scripts (`scripts/system_manager.py`, A15; `scripts/reconcile_positions.py`, A12).
- **Issue category:** Intended against actual (documentation against code); Failure handling.
- **Intended behaviour and source:** `load_token` docstring L51 (2026-04-17, `bcf03b5`): "Parse zerodha_token.json; return dict or None on any error (SU17)"; M41C SU17 L314 to L315 (2026-04-17): "load_token(token_path: Path) -> dict | None ... Parse JSON or return None on any error"; `is_token_valid` docstring L62 to L67 (2026-04-17): "Return True iff" the file exists, the account matches, the date is today (IST) and the token is non-empty; M41 SU17 L352 to L359 (2026-04-17): "Check file exists. Parse JSON. ... All must be true. Else invalid." [IS-71, IS-72]; the records' statement R02-65 (Record 02 L3497, 2026-09-18, DESCRIPTION; P12-S097, P12-S322; not inventoried by IS).
- **Actual code path:** `scripts/zerodha_login.py` `load_token` L49 to L57 (`except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError)`, L56), `is_token_valid` L60 to L77 (`token.get(...)` L74 to L76, `.strip()` L76); callers `main.py` L2362, L2547, L2553; `scripts/healthcheck_server.py` L38 to L46; `scripts/system_manager.py` L458 to L463; `scripts/reconcile_positions.py` L113 to L122.
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: `load_token` returns whatever `json.load` parses and catches only `OSError` and `JSONDecodeError`. INTERPRETATION (Python semantics; T1 to T4): a file that is not valid UTF-8 raises `UnicodeDecodeError` out of `load_token`; valid JSON that is not an object is returned as a list, string, number or boolean (`null` as `None`); `is_token_valid` then raises `AttributeError` at L74 for a list, string, number or boolean, and, when the account and the date match, at L76 for a `null` or non-string `access_token`; only a top-level `null` gives False (L70 to L71). INTERPRETATION (Python semantics; T2): a UTF-8 file with a byte-order mark parses as a `JSONDecodeError` and reads as `None`, the same as a missing file. FACT (callers): the health endpoint and the system manager catch any exception (`ok: False`; "check unavailable"); the live pre-load fails first for these shapes (`TypeError` at L2363, A01 C2), so the gate meets them only if the file changes between L2362 and L2547; `scripts/reconcile_positions.py` (A12) calls `.get` on the result at L117 outside any `try` in that function.
- **Evidence:** P07-S013, P07-S014, P07-S016, P07-S151; P12-S322; the lines above; T1 to T4.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (documentation against code: the helpers raise or return a non-dict where the contract promises `None` or False; failure handling). FACT; HISTORICAL (the dated sources); INTERPRETATION (Python semantics). KNOWN DEFECT considered and not given: (a) holds (the `except` clause is the mechanism for "any error"); (b) holds for these inputs (by Python semantics the exceptions escape whenever such a file is read); (c) fails: the documented writers write a JSON object with `json.dump`'s default ASCII output (`save_token` L170 to L172), and an empty or partial file reads as `None` (AU-20), so these shapes arise only from a foreign writer or a corrupted file, not under the documented set-up.
- **Severity or impact where established:** inside the trading process the effect is A01 C2's (exit 2 at the pre-load, KNOWN DEFECT for its parts, kept); none established at the gate; the health endpoint and the system manager degrade to "not valid"; the reconcile script's outcome is A12's.
- **Owner:** A04 (the helpers' contract); A01 (C2's handlers); A12 and A15 (their callers).
- **Cross-reference:** P07-S212 (point 17); STUDY 17.1 point 24 (P12-S322); A01 C2 (A04 boundary); CL-15; AU-20, AU-33.
- **Rama:** not needed to classify.

##### AU-02 — The browser login sends an empty request token without the re-prompt SU10 asks for; one parse failure of the exchange lies outside its stated `Raises`, and another falls under a class the list gives only for network failure

- **Area and flow:** token creation outside the trading process: `run_login_flow` and `exchange_request_token` (the login CLI; the interactive helper is unreachable, A01 C1).
- **Issue category:** Intended against actual; Failure handling (documentation against code for the `Raises` list).
- **Intended behaviour and source:** M41 SU10 f L229 (2026-04-17): "Validate input non-empty, re-prompt if blank."; SU10 g L231 to L235 (the exchange); `exchange_request_token` docstring L96 to L98 (2026-04-17): "Raises: RuntimeError: on non-200 response or missing access_token in response. requests.RequestException: on network failure."; `run_login_flow` docstring L208 to L209 (2026-04-17): "Raises: SystemExit(1): on exchange failure."; M41 SU19 L371 to L372 (2026-04-17): tests for "exchange_request_token: success, API error, malformed response" (TEST kind, documentary) [IS-71, IS-72].
- **Actual code path:** `scripts/zerodha_login.py` `run_login_flow` L222 (`input_fn(...).strip()`), L224 to L228; `exchange_request_token` L100 to L125 (`resp.json()` L119, `payload.get("data", {}).get(...)` L120).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: the pasted value is stripped and passed to the exchange with no emptiness test and no re-prompt (L222 to L225); an empty value is hashed into the checksum and sent. Whether the broker refuses it, and with which status, is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (broker behaviour); a non-200 answer raises `RuntimeError` (L114 to L117). INTERPRETATION (requests and Python semantics; synthetic tests of two later passes, `requests` 2.34.2 here; the repository pins `requests==2.33.1` in `requirements.txt`, and the library itself is outside the repository): a 200 answer whose body is not JSON makes `resp.json()` raise `requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError`, which in requests 2.27 and later is a `requests.RequestException` as well as a `ValueError` (so it falls under the `Raises` entry that the docstring describes as "network failure"); a 200 answer whose `data` member is `null` makes L120 raise `AttributeError`, which is outside the `Raises` list. FACT (the MATCH part): `run_login_flow` catches every exception of the exchange (`except Exception`, L226), prints "Login failed: <exception>" and exits 1, as its docstring states; the CLI is the only reachable caller in this part's files (the refresh's call, `scripts/auto_refresh_token.py` L226 to L238, is part TT's).
- **Evidence:** P07-S022, P07-S023, P07-S024, P07-S152, P07-S153; the lines above; the checker's synthetic test "test C1" and the corrector's "test K1" (section 1).
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (the empty-input check of SU10 f is absent; the `Raises` list omits one failure kind and misdescribes another), with a MATCH part (every exchange failure ends in "Login failed" and exit 1). FACT; HISTORICAL (the dated sources); INTERPRETATION (library semantics). KNOWN DEFECT not considered: condition (a) fails (no input check exists to fail).
- **Severity or impact where established:** operator-facing only, outside the trading process: an empty paste costs one exchange request and a re-run of the CLI (if the broker refuses it); nothing is written to the token file on a failed exchange (`save_token` runs only after it, L230).
- **Owner:** A04 (the login module); part TT for the refresh's use of the exchange.
- **Cross-reference:** P07-S212 (point 17); A01 C1 (the interactive caller unreachable); AU-23.
- **Rama:** not needed to classify.

##### AU-03 — The login CLI imports `core` at module level before its own `sys.path` insertion, so a standalone run needs the repository root importable some other way

- **Area and flow:** token creation outside the trading process: `python scripts/zerodha_login.py --account <ACCOUNT_ID>` (the documented standalone run; the PC morning scripts' call).
- **Issue category:** Flow and state (import order); Intended against actual.
- **Intended behaviour and source:** the module docstring L8 to L9 (2026-04-17; L9 cited by line only): "Can be run standalone"; M41 SU16 L340 to L350 (2026-04-17; L342 cited by line only): "Can also be run independently", "Re-login mid-session", "Running separately from main.py if operator prefers"; the CLI's own repository-root insertion before its `core` import, L254 to L256 (2026-04-17, `bcf03b5`); the invocations `deploy/zerodha_morning.bat` L45 and `deploy/zerodha_morning.ps1` L55 and `DEPLOYMENT.md` L183 (all cited by line only; part TT's files) [IS-71, IS-94, IS-95].
- **Actual code path:** `scripts/zerodha_login.py` L34 (`from core.time_authority import ist_timezone`, added by `f67a0c7`, DUP-1, 2026-04-27), L36, L255 to L256, L287 to L288; repository root at the baseline (`git ls-tree`): `core/__init__.py` and `scripts/__init__.py` exist, no `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, `pyproject.toml` or path file.
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: L34 runs when the module body runs, before `_cli_main` inserts the root at L255. HISTORICAL: before DUP-1 the module had no module-level `core` import (`git show f67a0c7^:scripts/zerodha_login.py`: a local `_IST`), so the order dependency dates from 27-Apr-2026. INTERPRETATION (Python start-up semantics; T9): run as a script from the root, Python puts `scripts/` first on `sys.path`, not the root, so L34 raises `ModuleNotFoundError` unless the root is importable otherwise (an inherited `PYTHONPATH`, a virtual environment's path setting); neither morning script sets `PYTHONPATH` (P07-S225). When `main.py` imports the module (root on the path) and when `scripts/auto_refresh_token.py` uses it (root inserted first, its L46 to L48), the import succeeds. HISTORICAL: the incident document runs the refresh with `PYTHONPATH=.` (`docs/05_incident_response.md` L209, 2026-06-03), a different script.
- **Evidence:** P07-S225, P07-S010, P07-S026; the lines above; `git show f67a0c7` (message: "Replace local _IST ... with core.time_authority.ist_timezone()"); T9.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (the CLI's own path insertion comes after a module-level import that needs it). FACT (order); INTERPRETATION (start-up semantics); HISTORICAL (the commit). KNOWN DEFECT considered and not given: (a) holds (L255 is the CLI's mechanism for importing the repository); (c) holds (the standalone run is documented and scripted); (b) fails: the import fails only when the operator's environment does not put the root on the path, which is not established.
- **Severity or impact where established:** if the root was not importable, every standalone login ended with a traceback and status 1 before the browser opened, and the morning scripts reported their login step as failed (part TT's texts); whether this occurred: UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (the PC's environment does not survive).
- **Owner:** A04 (the login module); part TT for the morning scripts and their environment.
- **Cross-reference:** P07-S212 (point 17); STUDY 17.1 point 14 (PC tools, part TT); A01 C40 (import-time effects); AU-23.
- **Rama:** not needed to classify; STUDY question 9 (whether the PC tools were still used, part TT) bears on impact only.

##### AU-08 — The token monitor decides "expired or transient" for every exception other than `TokenException` by its message text, so H-13's stated outcome for network, data and timeout errors is not guaranteed

- **Area and flow:** in-session token checking: `check_now()`'s exception branch → `_is_token_expiry()` → `classify_broker_auth_error()`.
- **Issue category:** Logic and calculation; Intended against actual (documentation against code).
- **Intended behaviour and source:** `_is_token_expiry` docstring L175 to L186 and comments L148 to L152 (2026-07-06, `e965589`, H-13): "True ONLY for a genuine token-invalid/expired signal ... False for transient errors (network/5xx/rate-limit — do NOT latch, do NOT soft_kill)"; "Classifies on BOTH the exception TYPE ... AND the message ... while a ``NetworkException`` / ``DataException`` / connection timeout classifies as transient and is ignored. An ``IP_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`` result means the token is VALID (do not fire)"; commit `e965589`: fire on "kiteconnect TokenException (matched by type name ...) OR auth_recovery.classify_broker_auth_error == "TOKEN_EXPIRED""; the legacy audit's fix direction H-13 (`docs/audit/full_system_audit_04july2026.md` L106, 2026-07-06): "only fire on `TokenException`-shaped errors, or require 2 consecutive failures" [IS-76, IC-20]. The classifier's own docstring L51 (2026-06-20): "Classify a BrokerAuthError (or its message)" [IS-77]; H-13, later, names the classifier and applies it to the monitor's raw exceptions.
- **Actual code path:** `broker/token_monitor.py` `check_now` L146 to L165; `_is_token_expiry` L174 to L193 (type test L187 to L188; classifier L189 to L190; its failure L191 to L193); `broker/auth_recovery.py` `classify_broker_auth_error` L50 to L64 (IP markers L28 to L37 first; token markers L40 to L47 or the bare substring "token", L62).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: the class test is positive only (a `TokenException` by name is always an expiry); every other exception is decided by `str(exc).lower()`: an IP marker gives "transient", a token marker or the substring "token" gives "expiry", anything else "transient". FACT (the MATCH part): the classifier is applied to the raw exceptions, as H-13 designs; a transient result logs the exception at ERROR with its traceback (`log_exception`, L147; `core/logger.py` L326 to L338, ERROR for any exception that is not a `TradingSystemError`, as the library's raw exceptions are) and one WARNING (L159 to L164), leaves the latch and sends nothing; H-13 states the WARNING, the no-latch and the no-kill; a classifier failure counts as transient (L191 to L193). INTERPRETATION (T8; the classifier's rules): a network, data, timeout or 5xx exception whose text contains "token", "api_key" or "access_token" and no IP marker fires the full expiry sequence (after the ERROR line that L147 writes for every failure: CRITICAL line, CRITICAL "TOKEN EXPIRED" notification, SOFT_KILL), contrary to "a NetworkException / DataException / connection timeout classifies as transient"; a `TokenException` whose text holds an IP marker fires too, because the class test comes first. FACT: the translated `BrokerAuthError("Zerodha token/auth failure: ...")` that the docstring also names cannot reach the monitor in the wiring (AU-06). INTERPRETATION: a persistent failure classed transient (a network outage) gives one ERROR line with traceback and one WARNING per interval in market hours and nothing else (P07-S067; P07-S078 omits the ERROR line).
- **Evidence:** P07-S067, P07-S068, P07-S070, P07-S078, P07-S082; P12-S305; the lines above; T8.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (H-13 designs a type test plus a message test, and states as an outcome that network, data and timeout exceptions classify as transient; the message test classes any such exception whose text holds a token marker as an expiry, so the stated outcome rests on the broker's and the library's wording), with a MATCH part (the classifier's use on raw exceptions; the transient branch). FACT; HISTORICAL (the dated sources); INTERPRETATION. KNOWN DEFECT considered and not given: (a) holds (the class test and the classifier are the mechanism); (b) fails: a misclassification occurs only for texts that contain the markers, which depends on the library's and the broker's messages (UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED, P07-S185).
- **Severity or impact where established:** not established; whether any transient message carried the markers, or any `TokenException` an IP marker, is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED.
- **Owner:** A04 (the token monitor and the classifier).
- **Cross-reference:** P07-S204 (point 9); P07-S207 (point 12, the application to raw exceptions); STUDY 17.1 point 10; STUDY section 13 row "Error classification" (pointer AU; CS-03); IC-20; AU-06, AU-13, AU-14.
- **Rama:** not needed to classify.

##### AU-11 — No in-session recovery: the running process never re-reads the token file or gives the client a new token, while the incident procedure expects the token monitor to "detect new token and resume"

- **Area and flow:** the token lifecycle after a rejection during the session: what the process does when the operator delivers a new token file; the token monitor's recovery branch; the account during the session.
- **Issue category:** Intended against actual (conflicting sources; a statement only the code contradicts, CD-26); Flow and state.
- **Intended behaviour and source:** on one side, TMON L20 to L21 (2026-05-30, `0cd1b14`): "Does not attempt to re-login or refresh the token automatically"; the April operator procedure (RUNBOOK T18R01 and PLAYBOOK P089 to P093, `docs/web_claude/06_live_operations/`, 2026-04-18; A01 IS-5.23): a soft kill, a new token on the PC, then a restart [IS-79]. On the other side, `docs/05_incident_response.md` L196 to L209 (lines 2026-06-03, `37e6698`): "Token Expiry Mid-Session", steps "Run `scripts\zerodha_morning.bat`", "Copy to VM", "3. Token monitor will detect new token and resume" (CD-26); M41 SU16 L344 to L345 (2026-04-17): the standalone login is useful to "Re-login mid-session if token invalidated" [IS-72]; HISTORICAL test plans (TEST kind) `docs/web_claude/07_crash_test/03_detailed_scenarios.md` L806 to L815 and L1321 to L1332 (2026-06-11; scenario IDs cited by line only): deleting or corrupting the token file while the system runs, then expecting "Token invalid detected" or "BrokerAuthError on API call", "SOFT_KILL + token invalidation". SPEC L145 (2026-04-17) names "auto-refresh" for a `token_manager` that was not built [IS-74]. No later source names the April procedure; none is chosen. No source states an in-session check of the broker-side identity.
- **Actual code path:** `main.py` L387 (the only live `set_access_token`), L2927 to L2929 (the feed's token from the environment); `broker/token_monitor.py` `check_now` L131 to L145 (the return value of `profile_fn()` discarded; the latch reset L139 to L144); `broker/zerodha_adapter.py` L399 (the client stored once), L367 and L408 (`account_id` "reserved", left `None` by `main.py`); `scripts/healthcheck_server.py` L36 to L46 (the only in-session reader of the file, A15).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: after the start no code in the trading process reads the token file for trading (only the health endpoint, to report), calls `set_access_token` on the live client, rebuilds the client or the adapter, or gives the feed a new token; the token monitor calls the broker, never the file. FACT: when a later `profile()` succeeds, the monitor logs INFO "token_monitor.token_recovered — expiry latch reset" and clears its latch, but makes no kill-switch call, so its SOFT_KILL stays (clearing it is A13's and the next start's, A01); such a success is possible only if the broker again accepts the token the client already holds. FACT: the profile's identity is never compared with the configured account; the adapter has no account identity. INTERPRETATION: a new token file delivered during the session changes nothing in the running process: the order paths keep the old token; a new token takes effect only through a new start; deleting the file while running does not by itself cause a broker refusal (the client keeps its token), so the test plans' expectation would not follow from the code.
- **Evidence:** P07-S041, P07-S077, P07-S106, P07-S134, P07-S135; P12-S305 (the latch); the lines above; `git grep` of `set_access_token` in non-test code.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (sources conflict on recovery after a mid-session token failure; the code follows the April procedure and TMON, and the June incident procedure's step 3 is contradicted by the code, CD-26), with a MATCH part (no automatic re-login or refresh, as TMON L21 states). FACT; INTERPRETATION. KNOWN DEFECT not considered: no reload mechanism exists (condition (a) fails).
- **Severity or impact where established:** not established; by the code an operator following the June procedure would see the system stay soft-killed with the old token in use until a restart.
- **Owner:** A04 (the token lifecycle and the token monitor); A13 (clearing the kill); A01 (the start that loads the token).

##### AU-16 — `get_server_time`'s local-clock fallback is returned as if it were the broker's clock: the start-up check then passes on any VM clock, and the probe records it as a skew sample

- **Area and flow:** the broker clock reading (the A04-owned matter of A01 C8 and C30 named by P11-S279): `get_server_time`'s fallback → the start-up clock check (A01) and the probe → the time authority's window (A01).

- **Intended behaviour and source:** LOCKED-YAML G4 L82 to L86 (2026-04-17): the "broker clock validated periodically via existing API call timestamps"; "Hybrid + log-only on skew" rejected because it "turns a safety check into a notification" [IS-81]; SPEC C.3 L668 to L669 (2026-04-17): "Extract response timestamp, compute skew vs VM clock" [IS-82]; PRELIVE BL-21 L3620 to L3631 and L3640 to L3642 (2026-04-21): the sketched probe is to return "the broker's response timestamp", but its body returns the local clock as a "placeholder" (L3629: `datetime.now(_IST)  # placeholder — check actual kiteconnect API`) and `None` only when the call raises (L3630 to L3631), and a sample is recorded only "if broker_ts is not None" (L3641); BL-21 thus leaves the no-timestamp case to a placeholder [IS-83]; on the other side, FIX-009's comments L1712 to L1714 and L1725 (2026-05-12, `31075d0`): "prefer broker Date header; fall back to local clock on miss" [IS-85]. FIX-009 does not name BL-21 or G4; none is chosen. No source addresses a fallback that the caller cannot tell from a header reading (evidence file, section 2.7).
- **Actual code path:** `broker/zerodha_adapter.py` `get_server_time` L1715, L1726 to L1728; `_install_date_header_hook` L1334 to L1350 (skipped silently without a session or hooks; a parse failure leaves `None`); callers `utils/startup_checks.py` L436 to L437 with `core/time_authority.py` L279 to L280 (A01), and `broker/clock_skew_probe.py` L110 to L141.
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: when no `Date` header was captured during the call (none sent, a parse failure, or no hook installed), the method returns `now_ist()` read after the call, as a bare `datetime` with no mark and no log line, indistinguishable from a header reading. INTERPRETATION (T7; the callers' arithmetic): at start the time authority compares it with `now_ist()` read just after, so the skew is about zero and the check passes whatever the VM clock says, confirming only that the broker answered (A01 C8 records this effect for the check); in the probe the reading minus the round-trip mid-point is half the call's elapsed time, which `record_broker_skew` stores in its window beside any header readings, so a window that mixes the two understates the broker skew, and a window of fallbacks only measures how long the calls took. FACT: whether the installed SDK exposed a session with hooks, and whether the broker's responses carried a `Date` header, is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (P01-S146, P07-S186), so how often the fallback was used is not established.

FACT; HISTORICAL (the dated sources); INTERPRETATION. KNOWN DEFECT not considered: no mechanism distinguishes the two readings (condition (a) fails). A01 C8 and C30 keep their classifications; this is the A04 record counted once, as P11-S279 asks.
- **Severity or impact where established:** not established; by the code, with no header captured, neither the start-up clock check nor the periodic probe can detect a VM clock error.

##### AU-17 — The value `get_server_time` returns can come from another thread's response on the shared session, not from "this call"

- **Area and flow:** the broker clock reading (STUDY section 13 row "Broker clock", owner AU): the reset and read of `_last_response_date` around the method's own call, with every other response on the one shared client.
- **Issue category:** Concurrency; Documentation against code.
- **Intended behaviour and source:** FIX-009 comment L1712 to L1714 (2026-05-12, `31075d0`): "the response hook (_install_date_header_hook) captures the HTTP Date header from this call. After the quote returns we use that header as the broker clock"; the hook's docstring L1327 to L1328 (2026-05-12): it captures "the HTTP Date header from each Kite API response" [IS-85]. No source addresses a value supplied by another thread's response (evidence file, section 2.7).
- **Actual code path:** `broker/zerodha_adapter.py` `get_server_time` L1715 (reset), L1716 to L1720 (the limiter's wait, then the quote), L1726 to L1727 (read); `_capture_date` L1341 to L1350 (writes the attribute with no lock); the shared client's users: the adapter's methods from several threads, the token monitor's raw `profile()` (AU-06), the historical closure when enabled (CL-06).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: only `get_server_time` resets the attribute; every response on the session that carries a parsable `Date` header writes it, from whichever thread made the request; neither the write nor the reset-and-read takes a lock. INTERPRETATION (requests' hook semantics, outside the repository; the interleaving): (i) when the method's own response carries a header, it overwrites any value written during the wait, and only a response of another thread landing between that response and L1726 can replace it, with a time of about the same second; (ii) when the method's own response carries none, or it fails to parse, a header written by another thread's response during the limiter's wait or the request is returned, earlier than the end of the call by up to the wait plus the round trip (or more, if that other request began before the reset), so at start, where the reference is the local clock just after the call (`core/time_authority.py` L279 to L280), the reading shows a negative skew of up to that size, and in the probe, where the reference is the mid-point (`broker/clock_skew_probe.py` L133), a skew of up to about half that size on either side of zero; (iii) a header from another response is still a broker `Date` value.
- **Evidence:** P07-S109, P07-S112 (c); P04-S340 (handed by CS); P05-S114 (handed by RL); P03-S035 (handed by RD); P01-S049; the lines above.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (minor; concurrency: the value is the session's last response, not this call's, as the comment states). FACT (no lock; one reset site); HISTORICAL (the dated sources); INTERPRETATION (the interleavings). KNOWN DEFECT not considered: the outcome depends on the interleaving and on which responses carry headers (condition (b) fails). The thread safety of the client and its session stays UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (P07-S189; A01 C38a, kept). Distinct from RL-11 (library thread safety, UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED) and CL-06 (the hook's silence), cross-part check XP.
- **Severity or impact where established:** bounded by the length of the call window (the limiter's wait, at most 30 s by default, plus the client's 10-s timeout); case (ii) needs responses that differ in carrying the header, which is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (P07-S186).
- **Owner:** A04.
- **Cross-reference:** P07-S210 (point 15); STUDY section 13 row "Broker clock" (pointer RL); STUDY 17.1 point 13; A01 C38a; CL-06; RL-11, RL-22; AU-16, AU-19; distinct from RL-11 (library thread safety, UNKNOWN) and CL-06 (the hook's silence), cross-part check XP.
- **Rama:** not needed to classify.

KNOWN DEFECT not considered: for the wrap, condition (c) fails, as in RD-03 (no source states which form the method was meant to deliver for the limiter's exceptions); for the 429's operation name, condition (b) fails, as in OA-06 (nothing fails but a label). New probe passes the RTT mid-point to remove latency bias from the skew measurement" [IS-84].
- **Actual code path:** `broker/clock_skew_probe.py` `_probe_once` L110 (`t_before`), L112, L132 to L141; `broker/zerodha_adapter.py` `get_server_time` L1717 (`self._rl.acquire(...)` for the `quote` category, before the request), L1720; the `quote` bucket's limits (3 and 3, `config/broker_limits.yaml`; its demand from the fill poll is RL-12's).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: `t_before` is read before `get_server_time`, which first waits for a `quote` token and only then sends the request; the reference is the mid-point of the whole interval. INTERPRETATION (T7, arithmetic with a perfect clock): a wait of W seconds shifts the reference W/2 earlier than the request's real mid-point, so a header reading shows a skew of about +W/2 (up to about 15 s at the default 30-s limit); with the local fallback (AU-16) the sample is about half the elapsed time. The latency of the network leg is removed as intended; the local wait is not. INTERPRETATION (A01's thresholds, `core/time_authority.py` L222 to L235): such a bias alone cannot bring the window's average to the 30-s HALT tier; it shifts readings toward the WARN and ALERT bands, whose callbacks `main.py` does not set (A01 C30).
- **Evidence:** P07-S110, P07-S120, P07-S124; the lines above; T7.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (the reference includes a local wait that is not part of the round trip whose latency the design meant to remove). FACT (the order of the reads); HISTORICAL (the dated sources); INTERPRETATION (the size of the bias). KNOWN DEFECT considered and not given: (a) holds (the mid-point is the mechanism) and (b) holds whenever the probe waits, but (c) fails: no source says the probe handles a limiter wait, and whether the probe ever waited for a token depends on the other `quote` callers at runtime.
- **Severity or impact where established:** not established; whether and how long the probe waited is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (P05-S166); by the code the bias stays below the HALT tier on its own.
- **Owner:** A04 (the probe).
- **Cross-reference:** P07-S211 (point 16); STUDY 17.1 point 13; A01 C30; RL-12 (the fill poll's demand on the `quote` bucket); AU-16, AU-17, AU-26.
- **Rama:** not needed to classify.

### 7.3 Issue and UNKNOWN records

##### TT-01 — The refresh's docstring gives 08:00 for its cron run, while the registry, the crontab, the script's own cron-entry docstring and the system map declare 08:15

- **Area and flow:** the headless refresh's stated schedule against the schedule declarations (A16) and the operator documents.
- **Issue category:** Documentation against code (and against configuration declarations).
- **Intended behaviour and source:** sources conflict (IC-25): (X) `scripts/auto_refresh_token.py` L6 (`ff0984b`, 2026-06-18): "Runs daily at 08:00 IST Mon-Fri via cron (after the 05:00 token cleanup)"; the FIX-187 commit `ff0984b` (2026-06-18): "so the 08:00 cron actually produces a usable token"; `docs/03_daily_operations_runbook.md` L19 and `docs/06_deployment_guide.md` L141 (2026-06-03): "08:00 Auto token refresh". (Y) `config/cron_registry.yaml` L198 to L211 (lines 2026-06-18 to 2026-06-23; A16 declaration): `schedule: 08:15 Mon-Fri`, `cron_expression: 15 8 * * 1-5`; `deploy/cron/trading-system.cron` L51 to L52 (generated; A16); the script's own `_cron_main` docstring L400 to L401 (`09ea725`, 2026-07-17): "05:00 delete -> 08:15 TOTP refresh -> token-watcher starts the app"; `docs/SYSTEM_MAP.md` L673 (2026-08-05): "08:15 cron → token file". The later sources do not name the earlier [IS-88, IS-89, IS-90, IS-95, IS-97; IC-25].
- **Actual code path:** `scripts/auto_refresh_token.py` L1 to L35 (docstring), L390 to L420 (entry); the declarations above.
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: the script sets no time of its own; it runs when invoked. FACT (declarations, not proof of a run): the only declared schedule is 08:15 Monday to Friday; the crontab has no `CRON_TZ`, so the declared time is IST only if the host's zone is IST (P08-S105). FACT: the module docstring and two runbooks state 08:00; the same file's later docstring states 08:15.
- **Evidence:** P08-S011, P08-S103, P08-S105; R03A-02 (records check); the lines above (`git blame`).
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (documentation against declared configuration). FACT; HISTORICAL (the sources). Sources conflict; the declarations follow Y. KNOWN DEFECT not considered: a docstring and runbook times are descriptions, not mechanisms (condition (a) fails). A03 G-11 mentions the docstring time as HISTORICAL only (not counted there).
- **Severity or impact where established:** documentation only; an operator following the runbooks' 08:00 would look for the token 15 minutes early; no code reads the text.
- **Owner:** A04 (the refresh's docstring); A16 (the schedule declarations); the runbooks are operator documents (A16 and A17 for the schedule they describe).
- **Cross-reference:** P08-S239 (point 1); P12-S325 (third part); STUDY 17.1 point 14; IC-25; A03 G-11.
- **Rama:** not needed to classify.

##### TT-02 — "A manual/ad-hoc run ... is never blocked", while the command line always passes the day guard: a run started from a shell on a weekend or a listed holiday exits 0 with no login and no token

- **Area and flow:** the refresh's entry and its day guard; manual token recovery outside the schedule (weekend recovery, verification runs, `--dry-run`).
- **Issue category:** Documentation against code; Intended against actual.
- **Intended behaviour and source:** `scripts/auto_refresh_token.py` `_cron_main` docstring L409 to L410 (`09ea725`, 2026-07-17): "The guard lives here, NOT in main(), so a manual/ad-hoc `main()` run (e.g. recovering a token on a weekend) is never blocked"; the S1 commit `09ea725` (2026-07-17): "The guard is in a new _cron_main per script, never in main(), so manual/ad-hoc runs on a weekend (e.g. re-issuing a token) are never blocked", and, in the same message, "The guard sits behind each script's existing `__main__`"; the operator documents give the command line as the manual route ("Or on VM directly ... `PYTHONPATH=. python3 scripts/auto_refresh_token.py`", `docs/03_daily_operations_runbook.md` L36 to L38, 2026-06-03; `docs/05_incident_response.md` L209). HISTORICAL. [IS-89; CD-29]

##### TT-03 — An HTTP error status is classed four different ways at the four HTTP steps, against the file's docstrings: retried as a network error at the password step, a rejection at the 2FA step, a definitive `_AuthError` at the connect step, an unretried `RuntimeError` at the session exchange

- **Area and flow:** the headless login's and the session exchange's failure handling (password, 2FA, request token, exchange) and the retry loop.
- **Issue category:** Failure handling; Consistency across components (within one file).
- **Intended behaviour and source:** the `_AuthError` docstring L75 to L77 (`ff0984b`, 2026-06-18): "Definitive authentication failure -- do NOT network-retry (e.g. wrong password, TOTP rejected after retry, request_token never returned)"; the `login_and_get_request_token` docstring L165 to L167 (same commit): "_AuthError: definitive auth failure (no point retrying). requests.RequestException: transient network/HTTP error (caller retries)"; the FIX-187 commit: "3x network backoff; 1x TOTP clock-skew retry"; the `run_refresh` docstring L249 to L252 (L250 to L252 `ff0984b`, 2026-06-18): "Transient network/HTTP errors are retried up to `_NETWORK_RETRIES` times with exponential backoff; _AuthError is fatal."; the exchange's own docstring, `scripts/zerodha_login.py` L96 to L98 (2026-04-17): "RuntimeError: on non-200 response or missing access_token in response. requests.RequestException: on network failure." HISTORICAL. [IS-88]
- **Actual code path:** `scripts/auto_refresh_token.py` L169 to L179 (password step: `raise_for_status()` L175, `resp.json()` L176, `_AuthError` only for a JSON `status` other than `success` L177 to L178, `data["data"]["request_id"]` L179); L181 to L210 (2FA: no `raise_for_status`; any status other than 200 is a failed attempt, L196 to L203; `_AuthError` after the second, L210); L123 to L146 (connect: no `raise_for_status`; an answer that is neither a redirect nor carries the token raises `_AuthError`, L142 to L145); `run_refresh` L248 to L273 (retries only `requests.RequestException`, L263); the session exchange: `_refresh_once` L235 to L237 calls `scripts/zerodha_login.py` `exchange_request_token` L84 to L125 (part AU's file; the refresh's call is TT's, AU-02), whose non-200 test is L114 to L117.
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT (code) and INTERPRETATION (library semantics; T3): an HTTP error status at the password step raises `requests.HTTPError`, a `RequestException`, so the whole sequence is retried up to three times (three WARNING records, then the failure path), and a wrong password answered with an HTTP error status would be submitted three times, each from a new session; a wrong password answered with HTTP 200 and a non-success JSON status raises `_AuthError` at once, the shape the unit test uses (P08-S029). An HTTP error status at the 2FA step (a 5xx included) counts as a rejected code and, at the second attempt, ends as `_AuthError` without a network retry, although L167 calls HTTP errors transient. At the connect step any non-redirect answer without the token (a 5xx or a 429 included) is `_AuthError`, as L77 ("request_token never returned") allows and L167 does not. A body that is not JSON is retried at the password step (`JSONDecodeError` is a `RequestException`) but is a failed attempt at the 2FA step; a JSON 2FA body that is not an object makes L198 raise `AttributeError`, outside the `except ValueError` (L200) and outside `run_refresh`'s retry, so the run ends at once; a password reply without `data.request_id` raises `KeyError` or `TypeError` (L179), not retried. At the exchange step (the fourth HTTP request of each attempt) any non-200 status, a 5xx or a 429 included, raises `RuntimeError` (`scripts/zerodha_login.py` L114 to L117), which `run_refresh` neither retries (only `requests.RequestException`, L263) nor treats as `_AuthError`, so it reaches `main`'s `except Exception` (L377 to L381) and the run ends at once with the CRITICAL alert, the FAILED heartbeat and status 1; a 200 reply without an access token is also `RuntimeError` (L121 to L124), not retried; a 200 reply whose body is not JSON is a `RequestException` (T3) and is retried with a whole new login (new session, password and TOTP) (P08-S181, P08-S182). Which statuses the broker gave for each failure: UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (P08-S230).
- **Evidence:** P08-S025, P08-S027 to P08-S030, P08-S032, P08-S033, P08-S141, P08-S142, P08-S177 to P08-S182; `scripts/zerodha_login.py` L96 to L98, L114 to L124; T3; `tests/unit/test_fix135_auto_token.py` L159 to L164 read as a document (A19).
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (failure handling: the same condition, an HTTP error status, is transient at one step and definitive at three; the file's own docstrings disagree, L76 to L77 against L167 and L250 to L251, and the code follows each at a different step; at the exchange a non-200 status is neither retried as L250 to L251 state for "Transient network/HTTP errors" nor classed as the definitive `_AuthError`). FACT; INTERPRETATION (library semantics); UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED component (the broker's statuses, which decide whether the password case ever occurred). KNOWN DEFECT considered and not given: for the 2FA case (a) and (b) hold (a 5xx at 2FA always ends as `_AuthError`), (c) holds (L167 says HTTP errors are transient and retried), but (d) fails (L77 classes a TOTP rejection after retry as definitive, and the code cannot tell a 5xx from a rejection, so not every source is contradicted); for the password case (b) is not established (the broker's statuses are UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED); for the exchange case (a), (b) and (c) hold (the retry loop exists; a non-200 exchange always ends the run unretried; L250 to L251 promise retries of HTTP errors), but (d) fails: L167 equates a "transient network/HTTP error" with `requests.RequestException`, and `exchange_request_token`'s docstring (L96 to L98) classes a non-200 answer as `RuntimeError`, separately from a network failure.
- **Severity or impact where established:** a transient server error at the 2FA, connect or exchange step ends the run without the network retries the commit describes; a password rejection with an HTTP error status, if the broker used one, costs three logins and about 6 s of waits before the CRITICAL alert. Whether repeated password submissions had any broker-side effect: UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED.
