### 14.3 Issue and UNKNOWN records

##### CG-01 — The calculator's stated purpose ("Used by the live engine (every order) and the paper engine") against costing only at a close, with no paper engine

- **Area and flow:** `broker/cost_calculator.py`: the stated purpose and users of the module and of `total_round_trip_cost`, against the non-test call sites.
- **Issue category:** Documentation against code.
- **Intended behaviour and source:** the module docstring L4 to L6 (2026-04-17, `bcf03b5`): "Compute itemized transaction costs for a single order leg. Used by the live engine (every order) and the paper engine (P&L simulation)"; L33: "Does not compute P&L (paper_engine's job)"; `total_round_trip_cost` docstring L255 to L257: "Total cost of a complete trade: BUY entry + SELL exit (CC12). Used by the paper engine for realistic P&L accounting (Project Rule 15)"; `docs/locked_decisions.yaml` CC12 L1271 to L1278 (2026-04-17): "Used by paper_engine for realistic P&L (Project Rule 15)"; P12 L333 to L341 (2026-04-17) lists `capital/cost_calculator.py` and `paper/paper_engine.py` among the files affected (L338 to L339), and P7a L295 to L302 (2026-04-17) lists `capital/cost_calculator.py` (L302) [IS-107, IS-108, IS-109; CD-37, CD-38]. Against (the consumers' own later texts): `orders/order_placer.py` L421 to L424 and L615 (BL-10a, "exit-path cost computation"); `broker/cost_calculator.py` L313 to L318 and `orders/order_reconciler.py` L322 to L326 (E4, 2026-07-17): the backstop close paths costed with the same calculator. HISTORICAL. `docs/audit/ADDENDUM_capital_drift_05-Aug-2026.md` L388 to L391 (2026-08-05, `b89147e`) records that an open delivery position's purchase costs are not booked ("it is unsold, so nothing is booked", L390; P10-S198), which agrees with the code.
- **Actual code path:** the only non-test callers: `orders/order_placer.py` L2347 (`round_trip_breakdown` in `_handle_exit_fill`), `orders/order_reconciler.py` L1356 (CHECK1) and L2460 (CHECK4), `orders/cnc_gtt_monitor.py` L572 (`_finalize_gtt_exit`), the last three through `round_trip_costs_or_zero` (`broker/cost_calculator.py` L340); `git ls-tree -r --name-only 970aabf` has no `paper_engine` module, no `paper/` folder and no `capital/cost_calculator.py`.
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: no non-test code calls the calculator before or at order placement; every call is at a close (an exit fill, a manual or partial close found by the reconciler, a GTT close), and only round trips are computed (no single-leg call). FACT: no paper engine exists; paper fills are synthesised inside the adapter (P02's paper-only range) and costed by the same close paths. INTERPRETATION: the "every order" text describes a per-order costing that the code does not perform; an open position carries no booked cost until it is closed.
- **Evidence:** P10-S011, P10-S012, P10-S043, P10-S049, P10-S090, P10-S198; `git grep` for `CostCalculator|calculate_cost|round_trip_breakdown|total_round_trip_cost|round_trip_costs_or_zero` (non-test, section 1.5 exclusions): the four call sites above, the t2 script's construction (A19) and the adapter's unused argument (CL-21).
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (minor). FACT; HISTORICAL. The module and CC12 name users and a timing ("every order") that the code does not have; the later consumer texts state the close-time use that the code has. KNOWN DEFECT not considered: texts, not a mechanism (condition (a) fails).
- **Severity or impact where established:** none on behaviour; a reader would expect per-order cost figures and a paper engine.
- **Owner:** A04.
- **Cross-reference:** P10-S162 (point 1); STUDY 17.1 point 18; STUDY 14 (documents against code); CD-37, CD-38; IS-107 to IS-109; CL-21 (the adapter's argument); CG-15.
- **Rama:** not needed.

##### CG-02 — Quantity and price are documented as "must be > 0" but never checked: a zero is costed as zero, a negative as negative charges, a missing value raises an undocumented exception, and on the normal exit path a missing entry price is costed as 0.0 without an error

- **Area and flow:** `calculate_cost` inputs `qty` and `price`, and through `round_trip_breakdown` the normal exit path's `entry_price`, `exit_price` and `exit_qty`.
- **Issue category:** Weakness (missing validation); Documentation against code; Failure handling.
- **Intended behaviour and source:** `broker/cost_calculator.py` docstring L127 to L128 (2026-04-17): "qty: number of shares (must be > 0)", "price: execution price per share (must be > 0)"; "Raises: ValueError: unknown side, product, exchange, or fno_kind" (L142 to L143); CC2 L1176 to L1177 (2026-04-17): "ValueError for unknown side or product" [IS-107; CD-44]. The principles "fail fast and loud ... no clever silent fallbacks" (`docs/chatgpt_project_clarification.md` L45 to L46, 2026-07-13; IS-39). HISTORICAL.
- **Actual code path:** `broker/cost_calculator.py` `_d` L82 to L84 (`Decimal(str(value))`), L166 (`turnover_d = _d(qty) * _d(price)`), L169 to L171 (`min(flat, proportional)`), no check of `qty` or `price` in L145 to L163; callers: `orders/order_placer.py` L2323 (`entry_price = float(trade_row.get("entry_actual_price") or 0.0)`), L2340 to L2341, L2347 to L2352; `orders/order_reconciler.py` L1345 and L2449 and `orders/cnc_gtt_monitor.py` L567 (positive entry price and quantity required before the call).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: no code checks the sign, type or size of either input. INTERPRETATION (T5, `decimal` semantics): a zero quantity or price gives every component 0.00; a negative quantity gives negative brokerage (the negative proportional value is the `min`), STT, exchange charge, SEBI fee and GST (T5: quantity −100 SELL at 500.00 gives a total of −32.02); a `None` or text value raises `decimal.InvalidOperation`, which the docstring does not list. FACT (normal exit path): a missing `entry_actual_price` becomes 0.0 at L2323 and is costed without an error: the BUY leg is all zeros and only the exit leg is charged (T5: 32.64 instead of 53.66 on the worked example), while the gross P&L is computed against an entry of 0.0 (L2363 to L2366) and `close_trade`'s ten-times ceiling is skipped when the stored entry price is NULL (`orders/order_manager.py` L588 to L593; A10's). FACT: the backstop paths guard a positive entry price and quantity (L1345, L2449; L567), and their exit prices come from resolvers that return only positive values (P10-S137); on the normal path neither the entry nor the exit price is checked before costing, and a malformed value fails in `float()` or `int()` before the costing `try` (P10-S136). INTERPRETATION: no caller-facing error distinguishes a zero, negative or missing input from a valid one; the documented precondition is left to each caller.
- **Evidence:** P10-S026, P10-S027, P10-S075, P10-S136, P10-S137; the lines above; T5.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (minor; latent on the backstop paths, reachable on the normal path only with a trade row that lacks `entry_actual_price`, which is A10's). FACT; INTERPRETATION. The docstring states a precondition and an exception list that the code does not enforce; a missing input becomes a silent zero leg. KNOWN DEFECT not considered: the calculator has no mechanism for these inputs (condition (a) fails); the precondition is stated, not handled.
- **Severity or impact where established:** none established; a missing entry price understates the charge by the whole entry leg.
- **Owner:** A04 (the calculator's contract); A10 (the normal exit path's 0.0 default and the gross P&L against it).
- **Cross-reference:** P10-S163 (point 2); STUDY 17.1 point 18; CD-44; IS-39, IS-107; CG-07 (the zero outcome of a failure).
- **Rama:** not needed.

##### CG-03 — Two unreachable branches in `calculate_cost`: the FIX-112 exchange check and the third F&O STT branch

- **Area and flow:** `calculate_cost` validation (L145 to L163) and the STT computation (L176 to L198).
- **Issue category:** Weakness (unused code).
- **Intended behaviour and source:** FIX-112, the comment L154 (2026-05-18, `6da0e6b`): "Validate FNO segment is only available on NSE", commit message "Add FNO segment validation (requires exchange=NSE, BSE has no FNO)"; the `fno_kind` check L160 to L163 (2026-04-22, `7ed3a3b`): "Must be 'FUTURES' or 'OPTIONS'"; CC2 (2026-04-17): only "NSE" is supported. HISTORICAL. No source states a purpose for an F&O STT branch other than futures and options.
- **Actual code path:** `broker/cost_calculator.py` L149 to L153 (any `exchange != "NSE"` raises), L154 to L159 (FIX-112: `is_fno and exchange != "NSE"` raises), L160 to L163 (`is_fno` with an unknown `fno_kind` raises), L177 to L189 (STT: FUTURES, OPTIONS, else `0.00` at L188 to L189).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** INTERPRETATION (control flow): L155 can never be true, because every `exchange` other than "NSE" has already raised at L149; L188 to L189 can never run, because with `is_fno` true an `fno_kind` other than "FUTURES" or "OPTIONS" has already raised at L160. FACT: FIX-112's stated rule (F&O only on NSE) holds through the earlier check, so the behaviour matches its intent; only the code that FIX-112 added is dead. FACT (blame): the dead `else` of L188 predates FIX-027's branches (`7ed3a3b`, 2026-04-22) and the FIX-112 check came after the general exchange check (`bcf03b5`, 2026-04-17).
- **Evidence:** P10-S024, P10-S031; `git blame 970aabf -L 154,190 -- broker/cost_calculator.py`; `git log -1 6da0e6b`.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (minor). FACT; INTERPRETATION. Dead code in a cost module (the weakness "unused code" of Document 04, section 5.3); no behavioural difference. KNOWN DEFECT not considered: nothing fails (conditions (b) and (d) fail).
- **Severity or impact where established:** none on behaviour.
- **Owner:** A04.
- **Cross-reference:** P10-S164 (point 3); STUDY 17.1 point 18; CG-04; CG-17.
- **Rama:** not needed.

##### CG-04 — The F&O costing (Audit #13, FIX-027) has no non-test caller; as written it would reject NRML for F&O legs, use the equity brokerage and exchange-charge fields for them, and take options turnover as quantity times price

- **Area and flow:** `calculate_cost` with `is_fno=True` and `fno_kind` "FUTURES" or "OPTIONS", the round-trip methods that pass these on, and the six F&O rates of `config/broker_costs.yaml` L24 to L35.
- **Issue category:** Weakness (unused code); Intended against actual (latent).
- **Intended behaviour and source:** the `is_fno` docstring L131 to L137 (2026-04-22, `7ed3a3b`, Audit #13): "when True, STT/stamp-duty use FNO rates instead of the cash-equity rates. Prevents phantom equity taxes on options/futures that would otherwise trip invariant checks (HARD_KILL)"; "Options STT is on premium, futures on notional"; `total_round_trip_cost` L260 to L261: "propagated to both legs so paper P&L reflects FNO statutory rates when trading derivatives"; FIX-027 (2026-05-14, `5dc8563`) comments at L179 to L223 and `config/broker_costs.yaml` L24 to L35; CC2 and the docstring L129: `product` "MIS" | "CO" | "CNC". ##### CG-05 — Every round trip is costed as a BUY at the entry and a SELL at the exit, so for a SHORT trade the sell-side STT and the buy-side stamp duty fall on the opposite legs

- **Area and flow:** `round_trip_breakdown` and `total_round_trip_cost` (no direction parameter), called for every close by the normal exit path, CHECK1, CHECK4 and the GTT close.
- **Issue category:** Logic and calculation; Intended against actual (a conflict between sources that the code resolves one way).
- **Intended behaviour and source:** the locked CC4 L1193 to L1199 (2026-04-17): "MIS/CO SELL: stt_sell_pct/100 * turnover; MIS/CO BUY: 0"; CC8 L1231 to L1237: "SELL side: stamp_duty = 0 always"; CC3 L1181 to L1186: "CNC BUY: 0 (delivery buy is free at Zerodha)"; `config/broker_costs.yaml` L16 and L21 to L22 (2026-04-17): STT "on sell-side turnover", stamp duty "on buy-side turnover". Against, for the round trip: CC12 L1271 to L1276 (2026-04-17): "Calls calculate_cost("BUY", qty, entry_price, product) + calculate_cost("SELL", qty, exit_price, product)"; `round_trip_breakdown` docstring L282 (2026-05-19, FIX-123): "BUY entry + SELL exit" [IS-107, IS-108]. No source addresses SHORT trades (evidence file, section 6.2, question 29). The sibling computations are direction-aware: the gross P&L (`orders/order_placer.py` L2362 to L2366, BL-10a, 2026-04-19, "Direction-correct gross PnL (EF-3)") and the daily report's fallback (`reports/daily_report.py` L351 to L353, 2026-05-19, FIX-125; A15). INTERPRETATION (T2, recomputation of the formulas as read): MIS, quantity 100, SHORT entry at 510.00 and exit at 500.00: costed as called (BUY 510, SELL 500) 53.44, with STT 12.50 on the exit turnover and stamp duty 1.53 on the entry turnover; costed on the sides traded 53.66 (STT 12.75, stamp duty 1.50); difference 0.22. For CNC the difference comes only from the stamp duty and the buy-brokerage exemption (T2: 130.01 against 130.21). The stored `cost_stt` and `cost_stamp_duty` of a SHORT trade on the normal path carry the attributions as called. FACT: six SHORT strategy files are `enabled: true` in the repository (`config/strategies/*_short.yaml`, `direction: "SHORT"`); whether they traded in Live is UNKNOWN (P10-S156; A07).

CC4 and CC8 tie STT and stamp duty to the side traded; CC12's round trip, silent on direction, fixes the entry as a BUY; the code applies CC12's wording to SHORT trades. KNOWN DEFECT considered and not given: (a) and (b) hold (the round trip exists and attributes the legs as stated for every SHORT trade); (c) not shown: no source states that the round trip handles SHORT trades (L255's "Total cost of a complete trade" names no direction), although every close path passes SHORT trades to it; (d) fails: the outcome agrees with CC12's wording (`docs/locked_decisions.yaml` L1274 to L1275: BUY at `entry_price`, SELL at `exit_price`) and with the `round_trip_breakdown` docstring L282, both intent sources, so it does not contradict every intent source.
- **Severity or impact where established:** small per trade (0.22 on the worked example; the sign depends on the prices); not established in production.

##### CG-06 — One calculator, three sources for its `product`: the normal exit path derives it from the order protocol (never "CNC"; an unknown protocol defaults to "MIS"), the reconciler passes the entry order's product and refuses to default, and the GTT close passes the literal "CNC"

- **Area and flow:** the `product` argument of every non-test cost call: `orders/order_placer.py` `_handle_exit_fill` (A10), `orders/order_reconciler.py` CHECK1 and CHECK4 (A12), `orders/cnc_gtt_monitor.py` `_finalize_gtt_exit` (A11); the calculator branches on it for brokerage, STT and stamp duty (CC3, CC4, CC8).

HISTORICAL. No source states whether delivery trades can be finalised through the normal exit path (evidence file, section 6.2, question 32).
- **Actual code path:** `orders/order_placer.py` L425 to L428 (`_PROTOCOL_TO_PRODUCT = {"CO_PLUS_TGT": "CO", "LIMIT_TRIPLE": "MIS"}`), L2328 to L2338 (unknown protocol: WARNING `order_placer.exit_fill_unknown_protocol`, "MIS"; intent from the product), L2347 to L2352; `orders/order_reconciler.py` L1282 to L1283 and L2436 to L2437 (`trade["product"]`, the ENTRY order's `o.product` through a LEFT JOIN, `core/state_store.py` L1445 to L1462; NULL when no ENTRY row joins; an unmapped product skips costing and release), L1361, L2465; `orders/cnc_gtt_monitor.py` L577 (`product="CNC"`, the trade row's product not read); the delivery strategies `config/strategies/positional_momentum_long.yaml`, `positional_sector_rotation.yaml`, `positional_swing_long.yaml` (`intent: "DELIVERY"` L10, `order_protocol: "LIMIT_TRIPLE"` L12).

KNOWN DEFECT considered and not given: (a) and (b) hold for the delivery case (the derivation exists and gives "MIS" for every `LIMIT_TRIPLE` fill); (c) is not shown: no source states that the normal path finalises delivery trades, and its reachability is A10's and A11's.

##### CG-07 — The fail-open zero: a costing failure books `charges = 0.0` and a gross `pnl_delta`, as E4's wrapper intends, but against the fund manager's NET-contract text, and the stored row carries no mark of the failure

- **Area and flow:** the failure branch of every non-test cost call: `round_trip_costs_or_zero` (CHECK1, CHECK4, the GTT close) and the normal exit path's own `try`; the charge then reaches `release_used(costs=...)`, the trade row and the reports.
- **Issue category:** Failure handling; Observability; Intended against actual (a conflict between sources that the code resolves one way).
- **Intended behaviour and source:** `broker/cost_calculator.py` docstring L313 to L329 (2026-07-17, `1f4509e`, E4): "FAIL-OPEN BY DESIGN: a cost-calculation failure must NEVER block a capital release ... So a failure (or a missing calculator) degrades to 0.0, which reverts that ONE row to the pre-fix gross behaviour, and is logged LOUDLY so it is attributable rather than silent. Mirrors order_placer.py's existing policy on the normal exit path deliberately — one policy, not two"; against, for the same case: `capital/fund_manager.py` L1225 to L1232 (2026-07-17, same commit): "EVERY production caller must pass the REAL costs from the shared CostCalculator. Passing 0.0 writes a GROSS pnl_delta, which silently breaks the "pnl_delta is NET" contract that the daily-loss limit, available capital, rehydrate and the reports all rely on. The 0.0 default is retained only for tests that model a zero-cost close" [IS-110; RS-09: the contract's decision record is held OPEN, status only]. The principles: "no clever silent fallbacks" (`docs/chatgpt_project_clarification.md` L45, 2026-07-13; IS-39). HISTORICAL. Same date and commit for both texts; neither names or replaces the other.
- **Actual code path:** `broker/cost_calculator.py` L331 to L337 (no calculator: ERROR `cost_calc_unavailable`, 0.0), L338 to L353 (any `Exception`: ERROR `cost_calc_failed ... context=%s product=%s`, 0.0); `orders/order_placer.py` L2345 to L2360 (any `Exception`: `log_exception`, ERROR `order_placer.cost_calc_failed`, `charges = 0.0`, `cost_breakdown` stays `None`), L2370 to L2378 and `orders/order_manager.py` L613, L651 to L656, L665 to L670 (`charges` 0.0, `net_pnl` = gross, six `cost_*` columns NULL); the backstop writers `core/state_store.py` L1857 to L1871 and L2457 to L2466 (`gross_pnl = pnl + 0.0`, `charges` 0.0; the `cost_*` columns never written, P10-S192); `capital/fund_manager.py` L1285 (`pnl = gross_pnl - costs`); `reports/daily_report.py` L953 to L975 (a closed row with `charges` 0 and NULL components shows zero components).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: on every non-test path a costing failure gives a zero charge, a `pnl_delta` equal to the gross P&L, and one ERROR line with the trade id; nothing in the trade row or the ledger row records that the figure is a fallback. INTERPRETATION (T5; the corrector's recomputation, quantity 1, equal entry and exit, rates of `config/broker_costs.yaml` L14 to L22): at the file rates a computed round trip is 0.00 only for a leg turnover below about ₹16.67 (MIS or CO; the brokerage, 0.03% of the turnover, is the first component to reach 0.01) or ₹5 (CNC; the STT, 0.1% on both legs, is the first), so at trading sizes a stored zero charge marks a failure, but no reader tests for it, and on CHECK1 and GTT rows NULL `cost_*` columns are normal, so they mark nothing (P10-S192). FACT (reachable causes): with a calculator wired by `main.py` (L3120, L3138) the `cost_calc_unavailable` branch has no non-test path; the calculator raises for an input it rejects, of which the only case the backstops' guards let through is an entry order stored with product "NRML" on CHECK1 or CHECK4 (CG-06; A01 M-30), a row that no code under `main.py`'s wiring writes (CG-06; CS-08), so whether one existed is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED; the normal path passes only "MIS" or "CO" and numeric values (CG-02). MATCH part: both paths apply the one fail-open policy that E4 states (zero, ERROR log, release not blocked); they differ only in what they keep (the normal path writes NULL components; the wrapper returns a total only).
- **Evidence:** P10-S051 to P10-S056, P10-S079, P10-S083, P10-S135, P10-S138, P10-S140, P10-S192; the lines above; T5.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (minor). FACT; INTERPRETATION; HISTORICAL. Two same-day sources disagree on whether a zero cost may be written outside tests; the code follows the wrapper, and the failure leaves no mark in the stored figures that the daily-loss limit and the reports read. KNOWN DEFECT not considered: the zero is the wrapper's stated design (condition (d) fails).
- **Severity or impact where established:** the day's net P&L overstated by the missing charge on each failed close; how often it happened is UNKNOWN (P10-S155).
- **Owner:** A04 (the wrapper and its contract); A10 (the normal path's branch); A09 (the NET contract's readers).
- **Cross-reference:** P10-S168 (point 7); STUDY 17.1 point 18; IS-39, IS-110; RS-09; CG-02; CG-06; CG-15; CG-23; A01 M-30 (part PR); related: PR-05, PR-07, PR-15 (distinct; the resolver's lookups and coercion, to which PR's section 2.3 row of A01 M-30 points; CG-07 counts the calculator's fail-open zero, which an "NRML" entry row would reach).
- **Rama:** not needed.

##### CG-08 — CHECK4 costs each partly closed slice as a full round trip, so the entry order's leg and its brokerage cap are charged again on every slice and on the final close

- **Area and flow:** `round_trip_costs_or_zero` called by `orders/order_reconciler.py` `_check4_partial_close` with `qty=closed_qty` (A12), followed by a final close of the remainder on another path; the calculator's per-call brokerage cap.
- **Issue category:** Logic and calculation; Intended against actual.
- **Intended behaviour and source:** the per-order basis of brokerage: CC3 L1181 to L1186 (2026-04-17): MIS/CO "min(brokerage_flat_intraday, brokerage_pct_intraday/100 * turnover)"; `config/broker_costs.yaml` L14 (2026-04-17): "Flat ₹20 cap per executed order (MIS/CO/CNC SELL)"; the schema comment `core/config_loader.py` L2117 (2026-04-17, A02's file): "flat ₹ per executed order cap". The slice rule: CHECK4 docstring L2367 to L2370 (2026-07-17, E4): "the closed slice is costed with the shared CostCalculator ... The costs are for the CLOSED SLICE only; the remainder is costed when it closes"; comment L2457 to L2459; `docs/audit/e4_w10_done_17jul2026.md` L109 to L110 and L175 ("costed on the closed slice") [IS-126]. HISTORICAL. No source states whether the entry order's charges were meant to be split across slices or charged once (evidence file, section 6.2, question 31).
- **Actual code path:** `orders/order_reconciler.py` L2433 to L2468 (on the cycle that owns the quantity compare-and-set, `round_trip_costs_or_zero(..., qty=int(closed_qty), entry_price=..., exit_price=..., product=...)`), L2470 to L2479 (`release_used(exit_qty=closed_qty, costs=charges)`); `broker/cost_calculator.py` L283 to L290 (a BUY leg and a SELL leg per call), L169 to L171 (one cap per leg per call); the later close of the remainder: `orders/order_placer.py` L2341, L2347 (the exit fill's quantity) or `orders/order_reconciler.py` L1281, L1356 (the reduced `qty_filled`).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: every slice is charged an entry BUY leg and an exit SELL leg, each with its own brokerage cap; the final close of the remainder is again a full round trip. INTERPRETATION (T3, recomputation of the formulas as read; MIS, entry 500.00, exit 505.00): quantity 1000 in one round trip 224.86 (brokerage 40.00); closed as 400 then 600, 272.06 (brokerage 80.00), 47.20 more; with the entry order charged once and the two exit orders each charged, 248.45; for quantity 100 (no cap binding) the slices differ from one round trip by −0.02 (rounding). The cap binds above a leg turnover of ₹66,666.67, so the excess appears only for larger trades. The exit slices are separate broker orders, so their separate caps follow the per-executed-order basis; the repeated entry leg does not, since the entry was one order. INTERPRETATION (P10-S193): the trade row's final `charges` cover only the last close, while the ledger holds each slice (A12's and A10's storage).
- **Evidence:** P10-S030, P10-S085, P10-S086, P10-S193; the lines above; T3.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE. FACT (a full round trip per slice); INTERPRETATION (the amounts). The E4 text "costed on the closed slice" is met literally; the per-executed-order basis of the brokerage cap is not met for the entry order, whose cap is charged once per slice plus once at the final close. KNOWN DEFECT considered and not given: (a) and (b) hold (the slice costing exists and repeats the entry leg on every slice); (d) fails: E4's own wording ("costed on the closed slice" by the round trip, IS-126) agrees with the code; the open intent is question 31.
- **Severity or impact where established:** up to one extra entry-leg charge per slice (on the large example 47.20 over one round trip); none for trades whose legs stay under the cap; how often CHECK4 ran is UNKNOWN (P10-S156).
- **Owner:** A12 (the per-slice call); A04 (the wrapper offers only a round trip, no exit-only leg).
- **Cross-reference:** P10-S169 (point 8), P10-S171 (point 10, NARROWED); STUDY 17.1 point 18; STUDY question 31; IS-126; CG-18 (the single cap per call for a one-order leg, MATCH).
- **Rama:** not needed to classify; question 31 bears on treatment.

##### CG-09 — The load-time rule "at least one of brokerage_flat_intraday or brokerage_pct_intraday must be > 0" does not fit the calculator's `min(flat, pct × turnover)`: either rate at 0 alone already makes every brokerage 0.00

- **Area and flow:** `config/broker_costs.yaml` `brokerage_flat_intraday` and `brokerage_pct_intraday` → the loader's validator (A02) → the calculator's brokerage formula (A04).

- **Actual code path:** `core/config_loader.py` L2155 to L2165 (each `>= 0`; error only if both are 0); `broker/cost_calculator.py` L169 to L171 (`brokerage_d = _r2(min(_d(z.brokerage_flat_intraday), proportional))`).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: the loader accepts a file with `brokerage_flat_intraday: 0` and a positive percentage, or the reverse. INTERPRETATION (T8): with either at 0, the `min` is 0 for every positive turnover, so every brokerage component and the GST on it are 0.00 (T8: flat 0 or percentage 0 gives brokerage 0.00 on MIS BUY 100 at 500.00; both positive give 15.00). The rule's purpose ("to be meaningful") holds only if both rates are positive under the consumer's formula. At the file values (20.0 and 0.03) both are positive and no difference arises.

The load-time check and the consumer's formula disagree on which values give a meaningful brokerage; A02 L-35's MATCH (the rule is enforced as written) is kept unchanged; the demonstrated mismatch lies in the validator's condition (A02's schema logic), while the calculator applies the locked CC3 `min` as written and no source states a rate guard for it (CC9, `docs/locked_decisions.yaml` L1243 to L1250); this record is a boundary issue owned by A02; A04 counts only its consumer side (an accepted single zero rate becomes a silent zero brokerage). KNOWN DEFECT not considered: no source states that a single zero rate is handled (condition (c) fails); no difference at the file values.
- **Severity or impact where established:** none at the file values.
- **Owner:** A02 (boundary issue: the validator's rule; L-35 kept unchanged); A04 side: the consumer applies CC3's `min` as written and turns an accepted single zero rate into a brokerage of 0.00 without a guard or log.
- **Cross-reference:** STUDY 17.1 point 18; IS-107; A02 L-35 (kept; MATCH, owner A02); CG-18; CG-20; related: A02 L-35 (distinct; a prior topic's MATCH that the loader enforces the rule as written, kept unchanged; CG-09 counts only the A04 consumer side of that rule against the calculator's `min`; no other A04 part records it).
- **Rama:** not needed.

##### CG-10 — The slippage model has no Live consumer and the calculator applies no slippage; its sources disagree on its role, with two more sources on the header's side than K-34 cites (A02 K-34, A04 side)

Live fills come from the broker; their price IS the truth"; the class docstring L52: "P12 paper-mode slippage applicator"; the records: "exists only for paper mode" (Record 02 R02-44, 2026-09-18; IS-117) [IS-112; CD-36]. (Zerodha rejects off-tick prices)"; the importer's: `orders/smart_tgt_manager.py` L729 and L753 (2026-05-14, FIX-044): "Snap raw_sl to valid tick using slippage_engine functions", "reuse slippage_engine functions". The leading underscore marks a module-private name by Python convention (the code's own naming contract). HISTORICAL.
- **Actual code path:** `broker/slippage_engine.py` L147 to L186; `orders/smart_tgt_manager.py` L57 (`from broker.slippage_engine import _round_down_to_tick, _round_up_to_tick`, `9be48f1`, 2026-05-14), L754 to L757 (called from `_modify_co_sl` at L570; the manager built at `main.py` L2973); `broker/zerodha_adapter.py` L115 to L120 (`7f93c2f`, 2026-06-16), L1112, L1114, L1443 to L1452 (CL-03's and OA's side).

KNOWN DEFECT not considered: a text and a naming matter, not a failing mechanism (condition (a) fails).

##### CG-12 — Tick rounding exists twice (the slippage module's helpers and `orders/price_math.round_to_tick`), the 0.05 fallback is resolved by seven separate tick functions and held both as `DEFAULT_TICK` and as a literal, against the stated "one source of truth per fact"

- **Area and flow:** STUDY section 13 row "Tick handling": the two Decimal rounding families and the tick sources that feed them on the Live order paths (the adapter's snap, the smart-target trail, the GTT placer, the breakeven, SL-breach and structure-exit managers, the order placer's emergency exit, end of day and the reconciler).
- **Issue category:** Consistency across components (duplication); Weakness (hardcoded value).
- **Intended behaviour and source:** `docs/chatgpt_project_clarification.md` L43 to L44 (2026-07-13, `5a71fb6`): "Derive, don't duplicate — one source of truth per fact (one resolver, one kill-switch authority, one tick-snap chokepoint, one config authority). Redundant copies drift."; `orders/price_math.py` L34 to L36 (2026-06-16, FIX-181): `round_to_tick` "mirrors slippage_engine's FIX-014 approach so SL/TGT prices and slippage rounding stay byte-identical", L43 to L44: "tick <= 0 falls back to plain 2-decimal rounding (defensive; a 0/neg tick is a config error caught at InstrumentCache load)", L23 to L26: `DEFAULT_TICK` "is only the fallback when a caller has no cache wired (recovery paths, tests)"; findings and recommendations (DESCRIPTION, not decisions): `docs/audit/integrity_audit_2026.md` IA-XDUP-03 L3640 to L3652 (2026-08-01): "the two Decimal tick-rounding families are same-semantics parallel implementations ... the money path (smart_tgt SL trail, adapter snap) rides the slippage_engine copy while price_math is the nominal home", recommendation "fold one family into the other (price_math as home ...)"; `docs/audit/audit_05jul2026.md` L113 (2026-07-06): "Extract `DEFAULT_TICK` ... to `core/constants.py`" [IS-113]. HISTORICAL. No later source records a decision on either recommendation.
- **Actual code path:** family 1: `broker/slippage_engine.py` L147 to L186 (three functions, no tick check); family 2: `orders/price_math.py` L30 to L57 (`mode` "up", "down", anything else nearest; `tick <= 0` gives `round(price, 2)`), used in `orders/price_math.py` L150 to L351, `orders/breakeven_manager.py` L280, `orders/cnc_gtt.py` L115 to L116, `orders/structure_exit_manager.py` L529; tick sources: the adapter's `_resolve_tick` (`broker/zerodha_adapter.py` L1383 to L1407; one WARNING per symbol; also handed to the GTT placer by `main.py` L3034, CL-10), `_tick_for` in `orders/order_placer.py` L4026 to L4034, `orders/breakeven_manager.py` L104 to L112, `orders/sl_breach_monitor.py` L72 to L80 and `orders/structure_exit_manager.py` L647 to L656 (silent fallback), `orders/cnc_gtt.py` L79 and L229 to L234 (silent fallback), `orders/smart_tgt_manager.py` L736 to L751 (its own literal 0.05 at L747, WARNING on every call); `orders/eod_squareoff.py` L1543 and `orders/order_reconciler.py` L2324 pass `DEFAULT_TICK` without consulting a cache (CS-10).
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** INTERPRETATION (T7, re-implementation of both as read): for positive ticks the two families give identical results (100,000 random cases over ticks 0.01 to 5.0 and the three modes: no mismatch); they differ for a tick of 0 (the helpers raise `decimal.DivisionByZero`; `round_to_tick` returns `round(price, 2)`), for a negative tick (the helper's "up" rounds down; `round_to_tick` returns `round(price, 2)`), and for an unknown mode string (`round_to_tick` silently rounds to nearest; the helpers have no mode). FACT: the instrument cache rejects a non-positive tick at load (`core/instrument_cache.py` L171 to L177) and every tick source above returns a positive value, so no difference is reached at the baseline (CG-27). FACT: the fallback is coded seven times with three different logging behaviours (once per symbol, never, every call), and on the order paths the value 0.05 is held twice (`orders/price_math.py` L27; `orders/smart_tgt_manager.py` L747); the instrument-master builder writes 0.05 as the tick of an unmatched symbol (`scripts/refresh_instruments.py` L181, L185, RI12 L25, 2026-04-17; A05), and the sizer's `min_tick_size` default is also 0.05 (`capital/position_sizer.py` L164 with `config/system_config.yaml` L229; A09; a different purpose).
- **Evidence:** P10-S115 to P10-S118, P10-S120, P10-S142; P04-S240; the lines above; `git grep -n "round_to_tick\|DEFAULT_TICK\|_round_up_to_tick\|_round_down_to_tick\|_round_nearest_to_tick\|_tick_for\|_resolve_tick"` (non-test, section 1.5 exclusions); T7.
- **Result and classification:** ISSUE (minor). FACT (the copies); INTERPRETATION (their agreement). The legacy's stated principle is one source per fact and one tick-snap chokepoint; the submission chokepoint exists (OA-37), but the rounding rule and its fallback are duplicated, and `price_math`'s "byte-identical" claim rests on two copies staying in step. No behavioural difference is reachable at the baseline. Related: CS-10 (distinct; CS-10 counts the exit price builders' rounding and its effect at the adapter's snap, `DEFAULT_TICK` at end of day and in the reconciler included; CG-12 counts the duplicated rounding rule and its fallback, and cites those two calls only as copies). KNOWN DEFECT not considered: the copies agree wherever they are reached (conditions (b) and (d) fail).
- **Severity or impact where established:** none at the baseline.
- **Owner:** A04 (the slippage module's helpers and the adapter's `_resolve_tick`); A09 (`orders/price_math.py`); A10 and A11 (the callers' own tick functions and the literal 0.05); A12 (`DEFAULT_TICK` at end of day and in the reconciler, CS-10).
- **Cross-reference:** P10-S178 (point 17, second part); STUDY 17.1 point 19; STUDY 13 "Tick handling"; IS-113; IS-39 (CLARIF); CL-03; CL-10; OA-36, OA-37; CS-10; CG-11; CG-27; related: CS-10 (distinct; the effect of `DEFAULT_TICK` passed without a cache at `orders/eod_squareoff.py` L1543 and `orders/order_reconciler.py` L2324 is counted there); related: OA-36, CL-10 (distinct; OA-36 counts `_resolve_tick`'s fail-safe contract as a MATCH and CL-10 its use by other owners as a private member; CG-12 counts it only as one of the seven fallback copies).
- **Rama:** not needed.

##### CG-13 — A second, private cost computation in the daily report recomputes the calculator's round trip with different rules (side-aware, MIS formulas only, `float` arithmetic, exchange charge and SEBI fee combined before rounding) and shows its components beside the calculator's stored total (A02 K-33, A04 side)

- **Area and flow:** STUDY section 13 row "Cost calculations": `reports/daily_report.py` `_compute_cost_breakdown` (A15) beside `CostCalculator`; the report's cost columns for a closed trade whose `cost_brokerage` is NULL.
- **Issue category:** Consistency across components (duplicated computation with different results).

Daily report rows match contract notes within rounding"; `config/broker_costs.yaml` L3 to L4 (2026-04-17): "All rates are applied by broker/cost_calculator.py"; CC9 (no hardcoded rates in the calculator); `docs/chatgpt_project_clarification.md` L43 to L44 (2026-07-13): "Derive, don't duplicate"; the report's own docstring L338 to L340 (2026-05-19, `b6cd512`, FIX-125): "Compute itemised Zerodha cost breakdown for a round-trip intraday trade. Private fallback for trades where cost_brokerage is NULL but charges total exists"; the report job "RETIRED 29-Aug-2026; module kept, runnable by hand" (`config/cron_registry.yaml` L543) [IS-109, IS-111, IS-114]. HISTORICAL.
- **Actual code path:** `reports/daily_report.py` L155 to L161 (its own `yaml.safe_load` of the file; errors swallowed), L337 to L381 (seven rates with literal defaults; `entry_side` from the direction; STT on the SELL leg and the MIS stamp duty for every trade; exchange charge plus SEBI fee summed unrounded, L367; GST on brokerage plus that sum, L368; `round(..., 2)` only on the round-trip sums), L950 to L971 (used when the row is closed, `charges` is set and positive, and `cost_brokerage` is NULL), L58 (`_CLOSED_STATUSES = ("CLOSED", "CLOSED_MANUAL")`); against `broker/cost_calculator.py` L145 to L300.
- **Actual behaviour and effective value:** FACT: the fallback has no CNC and no F&O rate and is direction-aware, unlike the calculator; it runs for exactly the rows whose components the calculator's result was not stored for, which are every costed CHECK1 close (`CLOSED_MANUAL`) and every GTT close (P10-S192, P10-S194). INTERPRETATION (T6, recomputation of both as read): MIS LONG 100 at 500.00 to 510.00: identical (53.66); MIS SHORT 510.00 to 500.00: report 53.66, calculator 53.44 (CG-05); MIS LONG 37 at 123.45 to 131.10: the combined exchange-and-SEBI column 0.29 against 0.28, sum 5.03 against 5.02 (rounding order); CNC LONG 10 at 1500.00 to 1560.00 (a GTT close): report components summing to 16.29 (STT 3.90, brokerage 9.18, stamp duty 0.45) beside the stored CNC total of 39.49 (STT 30.60, brokerage 4.68, stamp duty 2.25). So the report's components need not add up to the `charges` it prints for the same row, and for a CNC GTT close they come from the wrong product's table.

- **Result and classification:** ISSUE. FACT (a second computation of the same quantity); INTERPRETATION (the differing results). A02 K-33 ("ISSUE; FACT (rates held as literals in a second computation, against P12 and the file header). Not a KNOWN DEFECT"; Batch T5 group G2, AGREED) is kept unchanged; this record adds the A04 side: the calculator is not reused, and the second computation differs from it in direction, product and rounding. KNOWN DEFECT not considered: the report's choice of formula is A15's logic, and no source states that the fallback reproduces the calculator (conditions (c) and (d) not shown on the A04 side).
- **Severity or impact where established:** report figures only (the job is retired; the module is runnable by hand); none on stored charges or capital.
- **Owner:** A15 (the report); A04 side: the duplicated computation of the calculator's quantity; A02 (K-33, kept).
- **Cross-reference:** P10-S182 (point 21); P12-S343; P04-S345 (from part CS); STUDY 17.1 point 18; STUDY 13 "Cost calculations"; IS-109, IS-111, IS-114; A02 K-33 (kept); CG-05; CG-07.

## 17. Findings for discussion with Rama

Every finding is for the discussion with Rama after ChatGPT's review (Document 04, section 5.5); nothing is raised with Rama before ChatGPT has reviewed this AUDIT, and none is decided here.

(a) Established by evidence: the KNOWN DEFECTs first, then the other ISSUE items in part order (sections 5 to 14; their classifications are in each record; an item marked "also in (b)" needs Rama's intent as well; "(minor)" after an ID follows the record's own qualifier). UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED items are not findings established by evidence; those whose classification needs Rama are in (b).

- RD-01: KNOWN DEFECT (provisional until ChatGPT's review and the issue discussion with Rama). In `get_quote_raw`, a broker HTTP 429 freezes and counts the `order` bucket (the bucket of the order actions and the order-history polls), not the `quote` bucket the call took, so repeated refusals of raw quote reads delay order actions and are never reset by a successful quote.
- RL-03: KNOWN DEFECT (provisional until ChatGPT's review and the issue discussion with Rama). During a stop, the order monitor counts its own shutdown aborts (limiter waits cancelled by the shutdown event, no request sent) as broker API failures, so three aborted history polls fire the hard-kill callback during a graceful stop.
- MO-03: KNOWN DEFECT (provisional until ChatGPT's review and the issue discussion with Rama). The order monitor reads a `status_message` attribute that the order-history entry does not have (the broker's text is carried as `rejection_reason`), so every status change it publishes carries no rejection text.
- MO-09: KNOWN DEFECT (provisional until ChatGPT's review and the issue discussion with Rama). At restart, the rehydration moves a reloaded order only one step from PENDING, so an order whose first polled status is COMPLETE, CANCELLED or PARTIAL is refused by the state machine on every cycle: no fill event, no untrack, an ERROR each cycle.
- CL-01: The adapter's "single point of contact" claims against thirteen other kiteconnect importers and the raw-client flows.
- CL-02 (minor): ZA15's "kiteconnect>=5.1.0" against the exact pin that the start enforces.
- CL-03 (minor): ZA14's import list against the import from `orders.price_math` and the use of the slippage module's private rounding helpers.
- CL-04 (minor): `account_id`: IC9's per-order parameter implemented as an ignored constructor argument; the adapter holds no account identity.
- CL-05: Nothing at client or adapter construction checks the client, the mode or the credentials; empty keys and tokens reach the live client.
- CL-06 (minor): The Date-header hook: installed or skipped without a record, capturing from every response, with parse failures swallowed.
- CL-07: The live client is built from the primary row's key variable before, and regardless of, the broker pin and the row's `enabled` flag.
- CL-08: The live client's single timeout: `read_sec` is passed and `connect_sec` is never read.
- CL-09 (minor): The live client keeps the token of the first read; the L2576 environment write reaches only the feed, not the "broker code" its comment names.
- CL-10 (minor): Private members of the adapter used by other owners (the A04 side of A01 C36d).
- CL-11: Two sources for the API key, the environment and the token file's own `api_key`, never compared.
- CL-12: The eleven script clients choose the account and its credentials by at least eight different rules.
- CL-14 (minor): The T2 script's second adapter: options as documented, but no instrument cache, so its tick snapping rests on the 0.05 fallback.
- CL-15: Four script construction paths that handle other token-file problems let a malformed token file escape as an uncaught exception.
- CL-16: The AngelOne stub against its own docstring, the legacy audit's "fully built" sentence and the unread `broker` block.
- CL-17: No broker-adapter interface: the design's abstract `BrokerBase` was never built, and the callers are bound to the Zerodha adapter.
- CL-25 (minor): The live client's connection pool: the literal `HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=1, pool_maxsize=50)`, raised for the paper quote provider and carried to live for parity, with no key (the credentials, retry and shutdown as described: MATCH part).
- AU-01: `load_token` and `is_token_valid` against their contract: a non-UTF-8 file raises, non-object JSON is returned, and the validity test raises instead of answering "invalid".
- AU-02: The browser login sends an empty request token without the re-prompt SU10 asks for; one parse failure of the exchange lies outside its stated `Raises`, and another falls under a class the list gives only for network failure.
- AU-03: The login CLI imports `core` at module level before its own `sys.path` insertion, so a standalone run needs the repository root importable some other way.
- AU-05: Eight scripts read the token file themselves, outside `load_token` and `is_token_valid`, and use its token with no account or date check.
- AU-06: The token monitor calls the raw client's `profile()`, outside the adapter's limiter, exception translation and 429 handling.
- AU-07: The token monitor's cadence is a literal in `main.py`, and its first check comes one full interval (1,800 s) after it starts; also in (b).
- AU-08: The token monitor decides "expired or transient" for every exception other than `TokenException` by its message text, so H-13's stated outcome for network, data and timeout errors is not guaranteed.
- AU-09: The expiry latch is set before the soft-kill callback runs, so a soft kill that fails is not attempted again while the token stays rejected.
- AU-10: The token monitor's alert says the order monitor keeps managing stop-loss and target orders, while the order monitor stops itself and hard-kills after three authentication failures.
- AU-11: No in-session recovery: the running process never re-reads the token file or gives the client a new token, while the incident procedure expects the token monitor to "detect new token and resume".
- AU-13: The auth classifier tells a token failure from an IP-allowlist refusal by message text alone, and classes every "permission denied" as the IP case; also in (b).
- AU-14: The token monitor's module docstring and a code comment no longer describe the code: a trigger wider than H-13's, a `market_hours_only` option that does not exist, and a latch "once per session".
- AU-15: `get_server_time`'s docstring and the probe's "Honest Caveat" still say the live reading is the local clock after the round trip; since FIX-009 it is the captured `Date` header.
- AU-16: `get_server_time`'s local-clock fallback is returned as if it were the broker's clock: the start-up check then passes on any VM clock, and the probe records it as a skew sample.
- AU-17 (minor): The value `get_server_time` returns can come from another thread's response on the shared session, not from "this call".
- AU-18: `get_server_time`'s failures leave under another identity: the limiter's two exceptions become a plain `BrokerError` (the fourth method of STUDY 17.1 point 2), and a broker 429 is reported as `get_quote`.
- AU-19: The probe's "round-trip mid-point" starts before the limiter's wait, so a wait for a quote token biases every header reading by half the wait.
- TT-01: The refresh's docstring gives 08:00 for its cron run, while the registry, the crontab, the script's own cron-entry docstring and the system map declare 08:15.
- TT-02: "A manual/ad-hoc run ... is never blocked", while the command line always passes the day guard: a run started from a shell on a weekend or a listed holiday exits 0 with no login and no token.
- TT-03: An HTTP error status is classed four different ways at the four HTTP steps, against the file's docstrings: retried as a network error at the password step, a rejection at the 2FA step, a definitive `_AuthError` at the connect step, an unretried `RuntimeError` at the session exchange.
- TT-04: The second 2FA attempt waits 1 second, so it reaches "the next 30s window" only when a 30-second boundary falls between the two codes.
- TT-05: The refresh as the pre-flight's auto-fix: no overall time limit (about 100 s an attempt and 310 s for three at the nominal timeouts) against the fix's 120-second child limit and the engine's 30-second wait, under an engine contract of idempotent DB/OS-level fixes.
- TT-06: The refresh never configures logging: its INFO records (the success, the dry run, an unconfigured notifier) are dropped, so its cron log records failures but never a success.
- TT-07: A failed or missing refresh is signalled only by the refresh itself, and only when its notifier is configured and its run reaches its handlers; the watcher never alerts about a missing token; the sources conflict on whether the failure is observable (IC-26).
- TT-08: The refresh anchors its token and accounts paths to the repository root but finds its heartbeat database, its holiday calendar and its Telegram switch relative to the working directory.
- TT-09: The refresh's docstring says each credential comes first from "the account-specific env var named in accounts.csv"; two of the five names are built from the account identifier instead.
- TT-10: The token tooling selects the account by three rules: the refresh's primary row or any row by `--account` (enabled or not, broker untested), the morning scripts' literal account passed to the login CLI, and none in the watcher; all write or test the one shared file.
- TT-11: Five freshness tests in the tooling, besides the trading gate's rule, use different criteria, account tests and date bases, so components disagree about the same file.
- TT-12: The watcher's fresh-token test admits a token of another account, which the trading gate rejects, so the watcher starts a service that cannot pass its own gate.
- TT-13: A start refused before 08:00 (a clean exit 0 dated today), for example the boot start of the enabled unit, holds the watcher for the rest of the day, while `main.py`'s refusal message says the watcher will start the service after the morning refresh.
- TT-15: The crash branch's alert always says "restart backoff limit reached", also when no restart was attempted because the token was missing or stale or the hour was outside the window, and outside the window it repeats every IST day.
- TT-16: The watcher forces IST for its own dates but takes the unit's exit date from `systemctl show` in the host's zone and compares the two.
- TT-17: The watcher keeps its alert flags and its restart count in a folder under the host's `/tmp` that it creates only at start; if the folder disappears, the hourly cap stops counting and the once-a-day alerts repeat at every back-off poll.
- TT-18: The `.tmp` hold is silent: FIX-040 logged a line at every skipped poll, and FIX-188 removed it, so the indefinite hold that A03 E-47 records leaves no trace in the watcher's log.
- TT-19: The watcher's HALT alert and log line tell the operator to run `main.py --resume`, while `deploy/resume.sh` and the later runbooks direct the operator never to run `main.py --resume` directly on the VM (A01 R19).
- TT-20: The batch morning script's service check matches any answer containing "active", so an `inactive` unit passes and is reported as "Service: ACTIVE".
- TT-21: Both morning scripts check the service 15 s after the copy while the watcher polls every 30 s, so the check often runs before any start: the PowerShell script then reports a healthy start as a failure and opens an SSH session.
- TT-22: The PowerShell script calls itself the "PowerShell equivalent" of the batch file but tests the file's last-write date, not the record's date, and tests the service's answer exactly, not by substring.
- TT-23: Two runbooks tell the operator to run `scripts\zerodha_morning.bat`; the file is `deploy/zerodha_morning.bat`.
- TT-24: The incident procedure for a token that fails mid-session runs the morning script first, whose date-only test treats a PC token dated today as current, so it copies that same token again without a login.
- TT-25: The installer says it "Does NOT start trading-system directly" and that the service "waits for token_watcher trigger", yet enables the trading unit for boot, where it starts without the watcher's token or window test.
- TT-26: The operator card's control "stop the watcher and nothing calls `start_service`" does not allow for the pre-flight's Phase A auto-fix, which starts a stopped watcher at 08:30; the card names only the reboot hole.
- TT-27: The token file's daily deletion is declared for every day, while the design that introduced it deletes "on trading days" only (IC-18).
- TT-49: Both morning scripts tell the operator to check Telegram for a "SYSTEM START" alert; since 23-Apr-2026 the start alert the trading process sends is titled "System Active".
- TT-35 (minor): The refresh's network retry loop: the literals `_NETWORK_RETRIES = 3`, the 2 s and 4 s waits and `_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 10.0`, with no key (the loop as described: MATCH part).
- TT-46 (minor): The morning scripts' login and copy steps: each changes to a hard-coded PC project folder, an absolute path with no key (the steps as described: MATCH part).
- OA-01: HTTP-library timeouts and connection errors that reach the translator unwrapped become a plain `BrokerError`, not `BrokerTimeoutError`.
- OA-02 (minor): The class mapping is broader than ZA5 and blind to the operation: every `InputException` and `OrderException` becomes an order rejection, GTT reads and deletes included.
- OA-03 (minor): Local conversion errors: inside the `try` they are reported as errors "from Zerodha"; in the legs and triggers they escape untranslated.
- OA-04: `kite_status_code` is the exception's `code`, an HTTP status by the adapter's own comments, while the placer tests it for Kite's error codes 16388 and 16418.
- OA-05: `cancel_order` and `modify_order` apply no 429 handling: no bucket freeze, no counter advance and no reset.
- OA-06 (minor): The operation name given to the 429 branch: the GTT placement and modification report their 429s as "place_order"; names outside `_CATEGORY_MAP` default to "order" (the `get_quote_raw` instance is counted in RD-01).
- OA-07: Who repeats an action after a broker 429: RL6 and the PRELIVE BL-6 fix specification give the retry loop to the adapter; ZA11 and the BL-6 implementation keep it out.
- OA-08: `place_order` marks the internal order FAILED on every SDK exception, timeouts included, while the state machine's UNKNOWN_IN_FLIGHT, added for exactly that case, is never entered.
- OA-09 (minor): The state-machine entry stays PENDING when `acquire` raises after the registration.
- OA-10 (minor): `place_order` validation: ZA13's checks hold, before the token and the registration; the gaps beyond them.
- OA-11 (minor): Validation precedes snapping, so a validated positive price can be sent as 0.0.
- OA-12 (minor): The same "SL" limit is rounded past the trigger by `place_order` but to the nearest tick by `modify_order`.
- OA-13 (minor): The tick-snapping comments that no longer describe the code: "None = no-op", "No-op when no cache is wired" and "MARKET / SL-M: price is 0; nothing to snap".
- OA-14 (minor): Tags at the chokepoint: the adapter's comment gives a 20-character limit and says matching is "never the tag", against FIX-093 and the A-1/E-1 tag correlation; the cut to 16 makes the two MIS square-off tags one (A01 M-16, A04 side).
- OA-16: The protection band is opt-in at the chokepoint: only the MIS auto-square-off sends one, and every other MARKET request leaves the adapter without it, although the same change states that the broker refuses such orders.
- OA-17: Broker answers taken unchecked: `str()` of the order id, `place_gtt`'s "trigger_id" fallback and `get_gtts`' `list(res or [])` hide a missing answer from the callers' own checks.
- OA-18 (minor): The adapter's own contract texts that no longer describe the order actions: `place_order`'s "Raises" list, the `PlacedOrder.status` comment and ZA16's "state machine does via OSM7".
- OA-19 (minor): The CNC lock raises an `OrderRejectedError` that carries five of ZA6's eight context keys.
- OA-20: `cancel_order` and `modify_order` report a refusal, a timeout, a lost connection, a rejected token and a 429 alike as `success=False`, with only the exception's text to tell them apart.
- OA-21 (minor): Two failure-reporting styles for analogous actions: the order cancel and modification return a result, the GTT modification and deletion raise.
- OA-22: Varieties: `modify_order` always sends "regular" while the design trails a cover order's stop through it; `cancel_order` defaults to "regular" for callers that pass no variety.
- OA-23 (minor): Four statements say the adapter refuses OCO-GTTs while delivery is disabled; the later "R2 guard split" removed that gate from the GTT actions and left them unchanged (A02 K-05, A04 side).
- OA-24 (minor): `place_gtt` accepts a `tag` and uses it nowhere, so the callers' tags are dropped and a GTT placed under an unknown outcome carries no caller-chosen identifier.
- OA-25 (minor): No validation in the GTT, cancel and modify actions, and no tick snapping in the GTT actions, although FIX-181 calls the snap the net for "ALL placements".
- OA-26 (minor): The logging contract (ZA9): the GTT actions write no entry line and two of them no exit line; the 429 path raises without the traceback log.
- RD-02: Two order-book reads report their failures under the operation name `get_margins` (and `get_live_margin_pct` under `order_margins`).
- RD-03 (minor): The limiter's own exceptions reach callers unchanged from seven reads and as a plain `BrokerError` ("Unexpected error from Zerodha") from three.
- RD-04: Response parsing outside any `try`: raw Python exceptions, neither translated nor logged by the adapter, and one bad row discards the whole result.
- RD-05: `get_positions` turns a `None` or unexpected response, and five other list reads a `None` one, into `[]`, the same value as "no positions" or "no orders".
- RD-06: `get_margins` turns an unexpected response, or an absent field, into 0.0 with no marker.
- RD-07: `get_open_orders` keeps `OPEN` and `TRIGGER PENDING` only, while its own docstring and its callers use it as the list of orders that still exist.
- RD-09 (minor): A field present with the value `None`: three conventions across the reads (the string "None", passed through, or "").
- RD-10: `get_live_margin_pct`: a missing or zero `total` is returned, and cached for 300 s, as a valid margin of 0.0 (not reached in the `main.py` build).
- RD-11 (minor): `get_live_margin_pct`: every exception of the inner quote read, an authentication failure and a shutdown abort included, becomes a plain `BrokerError` (not reached in the `main.py` build).
- RD-12: `get_quote`: an absent price becomes 0.0 while absent optional fields become `None`, and some callers read the 0.0 as a price; a requested symbol missing from the answer is dropped without a signal.
- RD-13: Two quote wrappers over one SDK call with opposite keying conventions.
- RD-14: The reads pass their inputs to the SDK unchecked, against the adapter's ZA13 and ZA3 ("validation before rate_limiter.acquire").
- RD-15 (minor): ZA9's logging contract: four reads write no `call_start` or `call_end`, and a margin-cache hit returns with no log.
- RD-35 (minor): The `get_open_orders` docstring states CHECK 6's purpose as the reverse of RC5 (f) and of CHECK 6's code.
- RD-28 (minor): The margin cache's 300 s lifetime: a literal set in the constructor (FIX-072, "TTL = 5 minutes"), with no key (the cache and `invalidate_margin_cache` as described: MATCH part).
- CS-01: Two cancel helpers mark resting exits CANCELLED without reading the `CancelResult`.
- CS-02: A reconcile cycle ends at the positions, check-6 or G3 margins read on any failure other than a timeout or an authentication error, and that cycle's actions are not persisted.
- CS-03: The callers answer the same adapter exception classes in different ways: an authentication failure, a timeout, a broker 429 and a client-side limit each lead to different outcomes by caller.
- CS-04: Two callers decide an order's state from substrings of the cancel or modify `reason` text, with lists that differ.
- CS-05: The entry placement handles only `BrokerError` subclasses: the documented `ValueError` of `place_order` and the limiter's shutdown abort skip the order placer's failure path.
- CS-07: The live margin read has no wired caller, and the placer's 16388 invalidation always clears an empty cache.
- CS-08: `main.py` builds the reconciler without the order placer, so the in-flight recovery (the only reader of `get_all_orders` and of the placer's timeout queue) and the SL-check fallback never run.
- CS-10 (minor): The marketable-exit price is built in two ways for one gesture: the kill switch leaves the rounding to the adapter's nearest-tick snap, the other callers round away from the touch; three tick sources and two buffer sources.
- CS-11 (minor): The order placer reaches the one adapter by two routes, one through the protocols' private attributes, and its comment says it does not hold the adapter.
- CS-12 (minor): `get_gtts` hands the SDK's own GTT payload to the CNC GTT monitor, which parses the broker's schema itself.
- RL-01: No escalation of sustained broker 429s to a soft kill anywhere in the code: G7's 1 s / 5 s / 30 s / soft-kill ladder and `backoff_sequence_sec` are not implemented, while six texts still state them; single 429s reach kills only by other paths.
- RL-02: The limiter's outcomes at the two failure breakers: a client-side bucket timeout counts toward the kill switch's soft kill and the order monitor's hard kill, while a broker 429 is counted only by the hard-kill breaker.
- RL-04: The target manager takes its own `order` token before the adapter's `modify_order` takes another: two tokens for one broker request, and the two wait failures are counted differently.
- RL-05: The historical closure: the `historical` bucket is the only one with no 429 freeze path, and the closure's broker failures reach no translation and are swallowed by the fetcher.
- RL-06: No request limit is shared across processes: nine script clients use no limiter, three scripts build limiters of their own, and the shadow recorder's "SAME broker RateLimiter" claim does not hold.
- RL-07 (minor): Rate figures stated in texts that match no committed bucket: the adapter's "margins capacity (burst=1, 1/sec)", the architecture document's "Rate-limited (3 req/sec)" and the shadow recorder's "≤3 req/sec" for historical data.
- RL-08 (minor): The limiter's own texts that differ from its code: `_VALID_CATEGORIES` "used for validation and for iterating at construction", and an `acquire` contract that omits the shutdown abort.
- RL-09 (minor): A later, shorter `penalize` ends a longer freeze early: the freeze end is assigned, and the delay is computed under the adapter's 429 lock but applied outside it.
- RL-10 (minor): The limiter accepts any bucket values: a zero rate makes `acquire` raise an untyped `ZeroDivisionError`, a negative rate drains the bucket, and a burst below 1 refuses every call (the consumer side of A02 L-12 detail row 10).
- RL-16 (minor): `acquire`'s 30-second bound: the literal default `max_wait_sec: float = 30.0`, never passed, with no key (the blocking wait and its errors as described: MATCH part).
- MO-01: Unmapped broker statuses (the broker's transitional statuses among them) get no transition, no fill timeout and no escalation, only a WARNING every cycle.
- MO-02: The mapping uses the polled fill only on PARTIAL and COMPLETE rows: OM5's quantity rule is not implemented, and a fill reported on an OPEN-set row or on a CANCELLED or REJECTED row is not recorded.
- MO-04: The COMPLETE `OrderStatusChanged` is built from the watch entry before the final fill figures are known (A03 R-04's A04 side: the stale payload); the A04 side of A03 R-04's KNOWN DEFECT, kept as A03 records it; not a new A04 KNOWN DEFECT.
- MO-05: On COMPLETE, a zero broker quantity or price is silently replaced by the requested quantity or the expected price.
- MO-06 (minor): Every poll that sees PARTIAL commits a PARTIAL-to-PARTIAL transition and publishes `OrderStatusChanged`, whether or not the quantity grew.
- MO-07: The two failure counters count failed polls across all orders, not cycles: the threshold can be reached in one cycle and the critical callback repeats in it, timeouts are never counted or bounded, and one persistently failing order is masked by the others' successes.
- MO-08: `_safe_transition` re-raises a refused transition whenever either state is non-terminal (FIX-052), against OM12 and its own docstring; the refusal repeats every cycle and skips the rest of the handler.
- MO-10 (minor): The PENDING to SUBMITTED to OPEN auto-step commits two transitions without publishing `OrderStatusChanged` (A01 M-12's A04 side).
- MO-12: Cancel finalisation: no path re-reads the broker after a cancel, every cancel-time event carries the last polled figures, and four of the six paths never publish `OrderPartiallyTerminated`.
- MO-13: A failed or timed-out cancel is handled six different ways; on the two PARTIAL paths the order is dropped from polling with no transition and no report of its known partial fill.
- MO-15 (minor): `_handle_open` runs the reward-to-risk check after the fill-timeout check without testing whether the order was just cancelled, so the same order can be cancelled twice in one poll.
- MO-16: The stuck-PARTIAL timeout has three descriptions that disagree with each other and with the code; the six paths test the leg in four different ways.
- MO-17: The force close's "once per calendar day" lives only in memory and fires again after a restart past the configured time; three texts still promise that it closes positions; it cancels without reading each order's status.
- MO-19: The orphan callback as wired: the monitor passes `(internal id, broker id)` to a callback that takes `(order_id, reason)`, gives no cause, and calls it before untracking; the H-15 comment describes a reservation release that the wired callback does not make.
- MO-20: During a graceful shutdown the main thread's ENTRY cancels and the still-running poll thread act on the same watch entries without coordination.
- MO-22 (minor): The monitor's own texts describe less, or other, than its code: the callbacks' triggers, the crashed-PENDING handling, the self-stop, OM16's users and the shutdown summary's count.
- MO-23 (minor): The state machine's texts: "Single source of truth" for a machine no component reads, "8" states for nine, a pointer to a function that does not exist, a "reconciler resolves" row no reconciler reaches, and an EOD holder that never calls it.
- MO-24: EXPIRED: OM1 says the monitor handles it, and the state machine and the consumers' sets carry it, but nothing maps a broker status to it or requests it.
- MO-25: Status vocabularies and sets across files: three vocabularies, four "broker open" sets with three memberships, differing terminal and "still open" sets, and each file writing its own literals (STUDY section 13, "Status mappings").
- MO-26: Publish failures and the idempotent return: a raising `OrderFilled` subscriber leaves the completed order watched for the rest of the run, and a raising `OrderPartiallyTerminated` subscriber gets the event again every cycle (A01 C29 (c) and M-08's A04 side).
- MO-27 (minor): The watch entry's `auth_fail_count` field, commented as OM11's counter, is never read or written.
- MO-46 (minor): The monitor's two fixed thresholds: the authentication breaker's literal 3 (A01 C23 (e)'s A04 side) and the empty-history orphan count's literal 3 are not configurable, while the sibling general breaker is.
- MO-49 (minor): After `stop()` the poll thread can still be mid-cycle: the 5-second join is not checked or reported, and the cycle does not test the stop request between orders.
- PR-01: The resolver is declared the single source of product codes, but two A04 order paths act on the literal "CNC": the delivery lock compares it and every OCO-GTT sends it (A02 K-06, A04 side).
- PR-02 (minor): Construction checks only that the map is non-empty and holds dictionaries: a map without an intent the system uses, with unknown intent keys, or with a misspelt code is accepted at start and found only at first use, or never.
- PR-03 (minor): The FIX-115 comment calls the configuration object "Pydantic, immutable" and labels the defensive copy "(PR9)"; the schema is not frozen and PR9 is the import rule.
- PR-04 (minor): Exception types for an unknown intent and an unknown broker: the adapter's specification says an unknown intent raises `ProductNotSupportedError`, the resolver's decisions say `ValueError`, and `intent_for` answers an unknown broker with `ValueError` where `resolve` raises `ProductNotSupportedError`.
- PR-05: The resolver's reverse lookup (PR5, "used by order_reconciler") has no caller; the reverse mapping in use is the literal `PRODUCT_TO_INTENT`, which is not derived from `product_map` and differs from it in NRML and the empty code.
- PR-06 (minor): `intent_for("")` returns "BRACKET_ORDER" instead of raising, because the loop compares the empty "not supported" code like any other (latent: no caller).
- PR-07: While `force_intraday_only` is on, `place_order` coerces every intent other than the exact string "INTRADAY" to INTRADAY before the resolver runs: unknown intents and exits of positions held under another product included.
- PR-08: One order, two resolutions: the adapter resolves the coerced intent for the order it sends, while the screener gate and the order placer's `orders` rows resolve the uncoerced intent again and ignore `PlacedOrder.product`; with the coercion on, the stored and sent codes differ for an order whose intent is not INTRADAY (an exit of a trade held under another product), and a row's resolution can fail after the broker order exists.
- PR-09: Variety and product are never checked against each other: a Cover Order entry is resolved to "MIS" or "CNC" with variety "co", while a stored "CO" product is resolved to "CO" and sent with variety "regular"; the components that recognise a CO order disagree on which field says so.
- PR-10: `broker_net_qty` nets every row of a symbol across products (and, having no exchange, across exchanges), while each caller exits under one product's intent; the recorded #2e defect is unchanged at the baseline, and the retry of a swept row also passes through it.
- PR-11: The helpers discard a failed positions read without any record, and their fallback result cannot be told from a broker-confirmed one; the reader they replaced logged the failure.
- PR-12 (minor): `cancel_co_bracket`'s docstring says a raising `cancel_order` reaches end of day's generic handler; the Live `cancel_order` raises only the limiter's two exceptions, of which one goes to a different handler, and returns every kite-level failure as `success=False`.
- PR-13: A symbol's broker position is derived by at least four rules: the helper sums every row, end of day keeps the last intraday row's absolute quantity, the reconciler keeps the last row, and the kill switch's `_is_position_flat` reads the first row only, is unused, and is still named by the helper's docstring as the rule it matches.
- PR-24 (minor): The `place_order` docstring's step list puts the rate-limit token before the product resolution and the state-machine registration; the code resolves, applies the lock and registers first (added after the check, omission O-1).
- CG-01 (minor): The calculator's stated purpose ("Used by the live engine (every order) and the paper engine") against costing only at a close, with no paper engine.
- CG-02 (minor): Quantity and price are documented as "must be > 0" but never checked: a zero is costed as zero, a negative as negative charges, a missing value raises an undocumented exception, and on the normal exit path a missing entry price is costed as 0.0 without an error.
- CG-03 (minor): Two unreachable branches in `calculate_cost`: the FIX-112 exchange check and the third F&O STT branch.
- CG-04 (minor): The F&O costing (Audit #13, FIX-027) has no non-test caller; as written it would reject NRML for F&O legs, use the equity brokerage and exchange-charge fields for them, and take options turnover as quantity times price.
- CG-05: Every round trip is costed as a BUY at the entry and a SELL at the exit, so for a SHORT trade the sell-side STT and the buy-side stamp duty fall on the opposite legs.
- CG-06: One calculator, three sources for its `product`: the normal exit path derives it from the order protocol (never "CNC"; an unknown protocol defaults to "MIS"), the reconciler passes the entry order's product and refuses to default, and the GTT close passes the literal "CNC".
- CG-07 (minor): The fail-open zero: a costing failure books `charges = 0.0` and a gross `pnl_delta`, as E4's wrapper intends, but against the fund manager's NET-contract text, and the stored row carries no mark of the failure.
- CG-08: CHECK4 costs each partly closed slice as a full round trip, so the entry order's leg and its brokerage cap are charged again on every slice and on the final close.
- CG-09 (minor): The load-time rule "at least one of brokerage_flat_intraday or brokerage_pct_intraday must be > 0" does not fit the calculator's `min(flat, pct × turnover)`: either rate at 0 alone already makes every brokerage 0.00.
- CG-10: The slippage model has no Live consumer and the calculator applies no slippage; its sources disagree on its role, with two more sources on the header's side than K-34 cites (A02 K-34, A04 side).
- CG-11 (minor): The slippage module says it "Does not handle live mode", yet its three private rounding helpers are Live order-path code, imported under their underscore names by the smart-target manager and the adapter.
- CG-12 (minor): Tick rounding exists twice (the slippage module's helpers and `orders/price_math.round_to_tick`), the 0.05 fallback is resolved by seven separate tick functions and held both as `DEFAULT_TICK` and as a literal, against the stated "one source of truth per fact".
- CG-13: A second, private cost computation in the daily report recomputes the calculator's round trip with different rules (side-aware, MIS formulas only, `float` arithmetic, exchange charge and SEBI fee combined before rounding) and shows its components beside the calculator's stored total (A02 K-33, A04 side).

## 19. Coverage gaps

- Runtime: no broker response, token file, log, heartbeat, crontab, unit state or database row of the legacy machines survives. Whether any A04 path ran, with which commit (whether production ran any commit after `7d4970a`, so whether the market-protection keyword was ever sent), with which account, key and configuration values, how often the order actions met 429s, timeouts or token rejections, whether the limiter waited, aborted or froze, whether the token monitor, the probe, the refresh, the watcher or the morning and copy scripts ran and with what outcome, and what the broker answered, are UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (section 2.4; for example OA-15, OA-27, RD-08, RL-11 to RL-14, MO-11, MO-21, TT-14, TT-28, CG-14, CG-15, AU-04, AU-12). A schedule or unit declaration is never proof that a job ran (A16, A17). The legacy records' runtime counts (no broker 429 in 23 retained logs, the recovery paths unexercised, "0 executions ever") are HISTORICAL summaries, weighed for impact only.
- Synthetic tests: generic Python and library semantics were confirmed only with small synthetic tests written for this AUDIT (no legacy code imported, copied or run), on the work environment's Python 3.13.18 with `requests` 2.34.2 (the legacy pins `requests==2.33.1`): for example the `requests` timeout and connection exception classes and `str(None)` (part OA), `threading.Event.wait` and the freeze-end assignment (part RL), the token reader's exception coverage (part AU), `getattr` on a frozen data class (MO-03) and the order state machine's table on a hand copy (MO-09), a pydantic model configured like `SystemConfig` (PR-03), and the cost formulas re-implemented from the read code (part CG). Every such result is INTERPRETATION for the legacy machines, whose Python, `kiteconnect`, `requests`, `python-dotenv` and `pydantic` versions are UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (only the pin `kiteconnect==5.1.0` and the start's version check are code facts; CL-02, CL-18).
- Sources not in the repository: the `kiteconnect` library itself, so its exception classes and `code` values for timeouts, 429s and token faults, its timeout handling, its HTTP session and thread safety, whether it exposes `reqsession` and whether it accepts `market_protection` are UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (CL-18, OA-15, OA-27, RD-04, RL-11; intent-sources evidence file, section 7); the records' worktree at `e7bf477` with its uncommitted change set, which the five existing technical records describe and which is not in the clone (intent-sources evidence file, section 7; section 2.6); the broker's documentation of the period (status vocabulary, rate and tag limits, token lifetime, error texts) and its contract notes (CG-14); defining documents for many design and FIX labels beyond the passages cited; the three `.docx` operations documents (cited through the A01 intent-sources file) and the PNG captures, not opened. The long registers and audit documents were read at the search hits, not end to end; tests were not read (A19).
- Consumers not traced: the internals of the owner topics' consumers of broker results and exceptions (for example the order placer's retries and 16388 branch, A10; the reconciler's checks and its in-flight recovery, A12; the kill switch's breakers and flatten, A13; the sizer, A09; the GTT and smart-target managers, A11; the screener and entry gate, A06 and A07; the dashboard and reports, A15; the pre-flight, A20) are handed to their owners (section 15) as boundary issues or OPEN QUESTIONs for that topic; A04 audited only its own side of each.
- Each part's own list of what it could not establish, with the evidence that would settle each item: sections 5.7 (CL), 6.7 (AU), 7.7 (TT), 8.7 (OA), 9.7 (RD), 10.7 (CS), 11.7 (RL), 12.7 (MO), 13.7 (PR) and 14.7 (CG); and the intent-sources evidence file, section 7.
- Security restriction (D-07; Rama's standing instructions): no `.env` file, token file, key file or `*.local.yaml` overlay was opened; `config/accounts.csv` was read only for its column names and the environment-variable names it lists and was never used for checking; every repository-wide search excluded these files by pathspec once the exclusion was made general on 12-Nov-2026 (before that, one search displayed rows of two such files on a helper's screen; nothing from them was copied, recorded or used: section 1.5; part AU, section 6.1); passages that hold account identifiers, host lines, personal names or credential-variable values are cited by line only. Steps recorded as "stopped: security restriction": whether the literal default account identifiers in the scripts and the schedule declarations name the primary row (part CL, section 5.7; CL-12); whether the credential variable names were set in the VM's or the PC's environment files (part TT, sections 7.2.2 and 7.7); one operator 2FA document, examined only at its section D2 (part TT, section 7.1; intent-sources evidence file, IS-98 and section 7). No credential validity, history or exposure was investigated. A03's item G-19 is cited by its ID only (section 4).

- RD-03 and AU-18 (with RD-11): STUDY 17.1 point 2's methods that leave the limiter's exceptions as a plain `BrokerError` are reconciled: four methods by their own wait inside their `try` (`get_trades`, `get_open_orders`, `get_all_orders`, `get_server_time`), plus a fifth path, the inner quote read of `get_live_margin_pct`, not reached in the `main.py` build; RL-02 aligned (cross-part check XP, C-02).
- CS-03, RL-01, RL-02, MO-07 and MO-13: STUDY section 9 and 17.1 point 26 say that no code soft-kills on sustained 429s; the AUDIT adds the kills that broker 429s do reach: a run of 429s or client-side limits on the order monitor's history polls reaches the hard-kill callback after three counted failures; one 429 or client-side limit on a LIMIT_TRIPLE stop-loss leg reaches an emergency exit and a hard kill; one 429 on the monitor's fill-timeout or partial cancel, folded into `success=False`, reaches the orphan soft kill; the kill switch's auto-trip does not count the broker-429 class (XP, C-01).
- RL-02: added to STUDY 17.1 point 3 ("the kill switch's breaker counts limiter timeouts but not broker 429s"): no non-test code calls `record_success`, so the kill switch's counter is reset only at construction and the third counted failure since the process started soft-kills the system, not three consecutive failures.
